id: This Is Grief: On the Road-Martinborough Books & Post, 6 Kitchener Street, Martinborough 5711, Martinborough-Event Finder
name: This Is Grief: On the Road
venue: Martinborough Books & Post, 6 Kitchener Street, Martinborough 5711, Martinborough
long_description:
Grief is part of being human, but we still struggle to talk about it.

This Is Grief: On the Road is a free community event bringing honest conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them into communities across Aotearoa.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O'Connor for a relaxed, human conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the clichés, timelines and expectations we so often place around it. Kirsten will share from her own experience of grief and from her work writing and talking about loss, before opening the space for conversation and connection.

You don't need to have the right words. You don't need to share anything you don't want to. This is a space for anyone living with loss, or anyone who wants to better understand and support someone who is.

Come along, listen, talk if you'd like to, and be part of a conversation we don't have nearly often enough.

This is a free community event. Registration is recommended as places may be limited.

id: OvO (Italy) NZ Tour-Valhalla, 154 Vivian Street, Wellington-Event Finder
name: OvO (Italy) NZ Tour
venue: Valhalla, 154 Vivian Street, Wellington
long_description:
For many of us, music can be like a drug. At first everything and anything feels and is beyond amazing, but over time as our consumption increases, this magical euphoria wears off to a hollow and crushing emptiness. The now discerning music addict desperately searches for that new thing that will make them feel the high that they once had. But it gets harder to again feel this way. Until they stumble across something so unique, original, and idiosyncratic they cannot help but feel giddy, childish excitement.

OvO are one of those bands. Curiously infuriating yet dangerously exhilarating in their inability to be pigeon hold into genre or specific sound. Deftly navigating between noise rock, doom, extreme and blackened metal, industrial sludge and even electronica. “Decibel Magazine” have perhaps described them best by hailing the bands sound as “a David Lynch dance party”. Italy’s OvO, continue to rewrite the definition of what alternative music can be. Something which New Zealand audiences can look forward to seeing this October 2026.

Formed by Stefania Pedretti and Bruno Dorella in Milan, Italy in the late 90s. OvO have taken their inspiration from the likes of Suicide, Swans, and Diamana Galas. Centred around the ear piercing banshee-like vocals of Stefania, and a constant guitar drone and dark menace as the undercurrent of their songs. Bruno, equally essential in their music, pounds a stripped down drum-set as if he were the leader of an invading war party. Coupled with intensive percussion samples to help craft a unique and experimental sound.

With 25 years as a band, 11 albums behind them (including their most recent Gemma), over 1000 shows/festivals across the globe, and sharing stages with many of the biggest names in experimental music; Godflesh, Lightning Bolt, Thurston Moore, Sleepytime Gorilla Music, Psychic TV, Dillinger Escape Plan, Big Brave, Ufomammut, among others - New Zealand audiences have their chance to see one of the most unique and experienced bands still active.

id: La Dispute - No One Was Driving The Car Aotearoa Tour-MEOW, 9 Edward St, Wellington-Event Finder
name: La Dispute - No One Was Driving The Car Aotearoa Tour
venue: MEOW, 9 Edward St, Wellington
long_description:
The post-hardcore innovators of La Dispute, known for their emotionally charged lyrics and ambitious compositions, are hitting Aotearoa this October. These shows will celebrate their critically acclaimed fifth studio album, No One Was Driving The Car.

It’s been six years since La Dispute released their last album, Panorama. Since then, the Michigan post-hardcore band—made up of Jordan Dreyer on vocals, Brad Vander Lugt on drums, Chad Morgan-Sterenberg and Corey Stroffolino on guitar, and Adam Vass on bass—dealt with the stagnance of the pandemic, celebrated the ten-year anniversaries of Wildlife and Rooms Of The House, and began working on No One Was Driving The Car. The fifth studio LP is the first entirely produced by the group, and it came together in Grand Rapids and Detroit, the United Kingdom, Australia, and the Philippines: “I think the change in environment was really helpful to breathing new life into the process each time we came back to it,” Dreyer says.

Partly inspired by the 2017 psychological thriller First Reformed, No One Was Driving The Car reckons with malaise in the shadow of the looming apocalypse, which has noticeably been worsened by the advancement of tech. The title comes from a quote from a police officer Dreyer read in a news article about a lethal self-driving Tesla crash, an absurd event which raises questions about the amount of control we have in our own lives. In fourteen dynamic tracks, the band grapples with the existential topic and the human need to find comfort and a sense of security in an existence where we’re often thrust into chaos without permission. Dreyer yells with a more primal sense and sings in a more refined way, and the guitars have a sharper edge than ever before. “As much as I don’t enjoy the creative process because it’s taxing and often not fun, I also think it’s the most fun that I ever have,” Dreyer contemplates. “It’s the revelations you make, the breakthroughs. It’s banging your head against a wall and suddenly something clicks in a way that feels almost divine, like it came from somewhere else.”

id: Mini Mosaics - Taster Class-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
name: Mini Mosaics - Taster Class
venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
long_description:
Mini mosaics are really quick and simple to make - but can create a real design punch with colourful glass pieces and a set of three mosaics to make a “triptych” set.

You can have the finished items as either:
A triptych set on a backing board
A set ready to hang on a wall as singles
On a large sturdy jumpring ready to hang as a cute pendant set (or earrings).
On a cord for an heirloom Christmas ornament.

The class covers:
Preparing your bases and materials
Planning and choosing simple designs to make your mosaics really pop
How to snip your glass down into tiny pieces if needed (most pieces are already cut for you)
Working with adhesives, tips and tricks with tools.
Finally we will cover grouting and finishing your mosaics - including mounting options and more.

Some students may finish in time to grout your pieces - seeing these pieces are SO small, they are often dry enough for grouting. Or you can take your grout away to do at home, or leave with us to grout for you and collect in a few days. (There’s a small fee attached to that part.)

This is a warm and friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and those who want to begin to work with hand-cut glass terrerae.

All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.
Your materials for the class projects are supplied as part of your course fee.

Young makers aged 12 and up are welcome to join the class, as long as they are able to work safely with sharp glass and tools.

Anyone under the age of 16 must attend with an enrolled parent or caregiver who is there to support them and participate alongside them.

long_description:
A practical workshop that will introduce you to a structured and easy-to-follow method to take yourself into hypnosis and use it to your benefit. Let go of old habits and form new ones, brighten your future, excel in your career and create excellence.

Self-Hypnosis - Hypnotise Yourself

Self-hypnosis is a fantastic self-development tool. It can also be used for controlling pain, accelerated healing, letting go of limiting behaviours and a number of other applications. This workshop will provide you with a good insight into the world of hypnosis, demystify it and dispel the myths that surround it.

You’ll learn a structured method of taking yourself into hypnosis (informed by scientific research), some of the classic applications of self-hypnosis and evidence-based skills that will convince you without doubt of your ability to hypnotise yourself.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
• Define and discuss hypnosis
• Practice self-hypnosis
• Create and write hypnosis scripts for personal change
• Use the language of self-hypnosis
• Relax hypnotically to deep levels

Tea and coffee provided but bring your lunch, pen and paper.

name: Wairarapa and the New Zealand Wars - Peace and Portents
venue: Kiwi Hall, 62 Bell Street, Featherston
long_description:
Why did Wairarapa remain at peace during the New Zealand Wars? Explore the decisions, relationships and consequences that shaped our rohe.

Although Wairarapa saw no fighting during the New Zealand Wars, the conflict profoundly affected the region. Join Paora Ammunson, Papawai Marae kaumātua, to discover why Wairarapa became a place of refuge for those seeking safety, how peace was maintained, and the lasting consequences for local Māori communities and the district’s history.

long_description:
LOCAL SUPPORT FROM WELCOMER AND DEATHTRIPPA

Pōneke post-punks So So Modern celebrate the release of their new EP Light Years, their first new material in 13 years, with an early evening show at their local Newtown Community Centre.

So So Modern built their reputation as one of Wellington’s most renowned live acts through relentless touring alongside international acts like Foals, CSS, Deerhoof and Dirty Projectors. After an extended break the band returned to play new songs alongside old at Camp a Low Hum 2024 and more recently Great Sounds Great.

This special show sees the band perform live at the Newtown Community Centre, with the added bonus of being a great way to avoid election anxiety (ENROL TO VOTE).

With a sound built on complex and chaotic layering of synthesisers, guitars and rhythm, the band’s latest release Light Years shows clarity, restraint and simplicity. The limited 12” vinyl release by Flying Nun and Holiday Records is accompanied by the illuminating artwork by Lily Paris West on two exclusive colourways. To mark the occasion the band are also selling the first ever So So Modern T-shirts, featuring an exclusive design by all-time friend and national treasure, Toby Morris.

Capacity is strictly limited, don’t miss out.

See separate listing for the all-ages 3pm show the same day. https://www.undertheradar.co.nz/gig/104667/So-So-Modern---Light-Years-EP-Relief-Show-All-Ages---3pm.utr?mc_cid=9772bcae3d&mc_eid=c581fc1ab6

id: Son of Satan or prophet of peace? Hakaraia Mahika and the Tauranga War-National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Son of Satan or prophet of peace? Hakaraia Mahika and the Tauranga War
venue: National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington
long_description:
In his 1986 book 'The New Zealand Wars and the Victorian interpretation of racial conflict', James Belich noted that the nineteenth-century Bay of Plenty religious and military leader Hakaraia Mahika deserves more attention from historians.

Forty years later, Mark Derby’s forthcoming book 'Warrior Prophet – Hakaraia Mahika and the Tauranga Wars' proposes to provide that attention, along with an interpretive account of the New Zealand Wars in the Bay of Plenty, in which Hakaraia played a prominent and dramatic role.

Mahika was a key figure in the 1864 battle of Gate Pā, regarded by Belich as “arguably the most important battle of the New Zealand Wars.” He became a close and respected associate of Wiremu Tāmihana, Rewi Maniapoto and Te Kooti. Yet, today he is barely remembered outside his own tribal area of Waitaha-Tapuika, near Te Puke.

id: Visit the Upper Hutt Blockhouse - Wellington Heritage Festival-Upper Hutt Blockhouse, 1 Blockhouse Ln, Upper Hutt-Event Finder
name: Visit the Upper Hutt Blockhouse - Wellington Heritage Festival
venue: Upper Hutt Blockhouse, 1 Blockhouse Ln, Upper Hutt
long_description:
Tucked down a side street in Trentham, the Upper Hutt Blockhouse is a rare example of a building connected to the New Zealand Wars.

Peek through the balistraria, explore the exhibition, have a good chat with our friendly and knowledgeable team, and find out what became of the Blockhouse in the many decades after its use as a defensive fortification.

Drop in between 11am and 2pm, and stay as long as you like!

This rare opportunity to visit the Upper Hutt Blockhouse is proudly offered by Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga as part of the Wellington Heritage Festival 2026.

The open day is free to attend, but a koha is greatly appreciated.

Accessibility: Upper Hutt Blockhouse is a two-storey building with internal stairs and uneven surfaces, including a curb onto the grass and grass surrounds. The second floor may not be suitable for people with mobility issues due to the steep angle of the stairs. There is a drop-off point adjacent to the blockhouse for visitors with limited mobility. Unfortunately, due to the age and build of Upper Hutt Blockhouse it may not be accessible to people in wheelchairs. Our visitor hosts can share the history of our site with you from outside the building, showing you some of the features still on show from when the building was in use as a functioning blockhouse.

id: Kuratawhiti Heritage Loop-Greytown, Kuratawhiti Street, Greytown-Event Finder
name: Kuratawhiti Heritage Loop
venue: Greytown, Kuratawhiti Street, Greytown
long_description:
Kuratawhiti Street stretches between urban and rural settings and this guided walk will pause briefly at the boundaries at a number of significant buildings.
The walk skirts churches, parks, memorials and settler houses. Volunteers from the Greytown Heritage Trust will share histories and insights along the way.
At midpoint in the walk we will pause for coffee and pastries at Stable - a cafe set in a countryside garden. The last stretch of the walk is entirely rural, briefly touches the Waiohine and returns by a walking track formed from an unmade road. Against a backdrop of the distant Tararuas, we face expansive views across a farming landscape towards the eastern hills.

Participants will need sturdy walk shoes or sneakers with good tread.

The ticket price for this event includes a $10 donation to the Greytown Heritage Trust to develop their digital guide and $20 for a fabulous morning tea at Stable Cafe.

id: Hidden Lakes Explore and Learn-Hidden Lakes, Masterton-Event Finder
name: Hidden Lakes Explore and Learn
venue: Hidden Lakes, Masterton
long_description:
North of Masterton are 2 hidden lakes, formed when the 1855 earthquake re-routed the Ruamahanga River.

The old route was cut off by the earthquake and formed 2 small lakes.

id: Silver Clay Taster-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Silver Clay Taster
venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
long_description:
Join us to try out this amazing technique and make a gift for yourself or your loved ones :-)

Precious Metal Clay is an incredible product made from metal particles mixed with an organic binder. When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.

Beginners start with simple pendants/earrings. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!

Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Precious Metal Clay is the ultimate recyclable material!

Included in the course fee is 5 grams of fine silver clay, enough to make a pendant or earrings, or a collection of charms - it's up to you.

Extra findings such as earring hooks and chains will be available to purchase (you can also make your earring hooks if you are feeling adventurous).

This class is great for kids also but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany any person under the age of 16.

name: Royal New Zealand Ballet Presents the Sleeping Beauty
venue: St James Theatre, 77-87 Courtenay Place, Wellington
long_description:
To celebrate the summer, we return to a much-loved Royal New Zealand Ballet production from 2011: Greg Horsman’s fairytale version of The Sleeping Beauty.
The age-old story of the princess who pricks her finger and falls into an enchanted sleep, only to be wakened by true love, is brought to life in picture-perfect designs by Gary Harris, classical choreography and Tchaikovsky’s magical music. A touch of wizardry from Wellington’s Wētā Workshop adds to the joy and wonder, making this the perfect pre-Christmas treat for audiences of all ages.

More than 42,000 people saw the premiere of this glorious production around New Zealand in 2011. Choreographer Greg Horsman left the Royal New Zealand Ballet in 2012 to take up a new role at Queensland Ballet, and this production has now been staged there several times to great acclaim.

Book more than one show from our 2026 season through our ‘Subscribe and Save’ package, and save up to 20% on your tickets

name: A Talent for Murder - British and Irish Film Festival
venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Toronto International Film Festival -

British national treasure Helen Mirren plays The Talented Mr. Ripley author Patricia Highsmith in this deeply intriguing thriller.

A Talent for Murder takes place in 1995, with Highsmith now in her seventies - and in poor health. Retired to her secluded house in the Swiss Alps, the author keeps to her study, immersed in her books, accompanied by her cats, and surrounded by a collection of antique weapons.

Highsmith’s solitude is interrupted by the arrival of Edward Ridgeway (recent Tony-winner Alden Ehrenreich), a mysterious messenger from a New York publisher, sent to persuade the author to write one final instalment of the Ripley anthology. Aggravated by the unexpected visit from this youthful, overly eager envoy, Patricia declines the offer. That is, unless Ridgeway can help her in conjuring up the perfect murder story.

Mirren embodies the wickedly manipulative author with gusto, while Ehrenreich imbues Ridgeway with enough guile to keep us guessing at his motives.

From director Anton Corbijn (Control), A Talent for Murder is replete with brilliant twists, biting dialogue, and delicious entanglements. Direct from its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival, don’t miss this highly anticipated thriller!

id: Walk in the Dark Carterton-Carterton Golf Club, Chester Road, Carterton-Event Finder
name: Walk in the Dark Carterton
venue: Carterton Golf Club, Chester Road, Carterton
long_description:
This Walk in the Dark is held at the Carterton Golf Course.

Step into the beauty of the night with this unique offering for the Wairarapa Walking Festival. Hosted on the manicured grounds of a local golf course, this gentle evening stroll allows you to experience the magic of darkness without worrying about uneven paddocks or rough terrain.

As we walk together, the transition from dusk to dark will naturally unfold, helping us acclimatise to the night. For those new to walking in the dark, handy red-light torches will be provided to keep you comfortable. This is less about distance and more about slowing down, stepping slightly outside of your comfort zone, and embracing the calm of night.

Along the way, we’ll reflect on the value of darkness - its role in history, its impact on wellbeing, and its importance for the environment. We’ll then pause to share hot chocolate and, if the skies are clear, look up in awe at a canopy of stars. With star charts in hand, we’ll explore what the November night skies have to offer and why protecting them matters.

The evening concludes with simple, practical ways we can all help preserve our night skies - because our environment doesn’t end at the treetops, it stretches all the way to the stars.

id: The Fabulous Carmen Walk Tour: Tea, Toasties and Trade-Thistle Hall, 293 Cuba St, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
name: The Fabulous Carmen Walk Tour: Tea, Toasties and Trade
venue: Thistle Hall, 293 Cuba St, Te Aro, Wellington
long_description:
Entrepreneur, entertainer, madam and mayoral candidate Carmen Rupe was based in Wellington for less than 15-years but has left us a rich legacy of memories and inspiring moments.

Join us on this free 90-minute community walk-tour as we trace Carmen's Wellington years (1967-1980). We'll visit some of the remaining inner-city business locations and imagine some of those that are no longer here: Le Balcon, Carmen's International Coffee Lounge, The Peacock, Cleopatra's Coffee Lounge, Carmen's Bazaar, The Gazebo massage parlour, The Cottage brothel and Carmen's Curio Shop.

Learn about Carmen's landmark 1966 court case, her race to become Mayor of Wellington in the 1970s, and how she supported and offered a safe harbour to Wellington's Takatāpui LGBTI Rainbow communities.

“I would more or less hypnotise all my guests like a black widow spider and trap my clients caught in my web. As people left my coffee lounge at 6am or earlier I would splash them with Carmen’s exotic juice which meant that they would be back another night for more. The scent would guide them to me. Some would hear my voice calling like an eerie whisper from the depths of darkness.” [from Carmen’s autobiography, "Carmen: My Life"]

Accessibility information: The tour is on flat public footpaths. Tours are limited to around 20 walkers.

Time/Date: 1pm, Sunday 1 November, 2026
Starts: outside Thistle Hall, 293 Cuba St, Te Aro, Wellington,
Ends: Jack Ilott Green, corner of Harris Street & Jervois Quay (just by Civic Square)
Duration: 90 minutes
Cost / Bookings: the tour is free but you do need to register

PLEASE REGISTER AT https://walktours.nz/book/

venue: Pyramid Club, 272 Taranaki Street, Wellington
long_description:
DESCENDANTS BOOK TOUR

with Lee Hana, Ludus, Erika Grant, Junus Orca

Lee Hana, with friends and collaborators, is making an immersive soundworld for ‘Descendants’, his latest mind-bending collection of science fiction stories. $15 presales via UTR / $20 on door ($10 unwaged)
_____

LEE HANA. An Aotearoa-Australian writer in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington, Lee Hana’s writing has appeared in New Australian Fiction, Cordite, Dark Mountain, Overland and Antipodean SF. The story collection ‘Descendants’ was launched by PSY FI, a Pōneke showcase of future facing artists. lee-ha-na.com
_____

LUDUS. Intrepid electronic producer Emma Bernard is always moving between worlds: from ambient to field recordings, from Whanganui to Chengdu, from headlining festivals with her avant-industrial band BIRDPARTY, to the spiritual ambient explorations created by Ludus for diverse spaces such as Splore and O Vere Beata Lux at Erskine Chapel. @ludus.etc
_____

ERIKA GRANT. Erika Grant is an outer limits sound explorer and one of Pōneke’s great musical collaborators, from Orchestra of Spheres to Cookie Brooklyn & The Crumbs. @erika_grant31
_____

JUNUS ORCA. Joshua Holmes always find the human feeling in his versatile mix of electronic sounds, from noise, to ambient and dub-techno. @junusorca
_____

DESCENDANTS by Lee Hana. Mind-bending science fiction stories. ‘Mass hysteria overwhelms an Australian shopping mall. A Burmese monk recalls a strange path to enlightenment. A firebrand lawmaker discovers what’s left after her soul is stolen. And everywhere, in this wild panorama of the next five centuries, we find the spectral traces of ourselves. These are worlds, sometimes disturbing, where you may not recognise your descendants…’ Available now at Unity Books.

id: Duntulm Farm Wairarapa Dog Walk-Duntulm Farm, 820 Mangatarere Valley Road, West Taratahi, Carterton-Event Finder
name: Duntulm Farm Wairarapa Dog Walk
venue: Duntulm Farm, 820 Mangatarere Valley Road, West Taratahi, Carterton
long_description:
The Wairarapa Dogwalk Group is an informal group of dog owners who get together once a month to exercise our dogs. The aim of the walks is to go somewhere in the region where we can walk the dogs off lead.
The Duntulm Farm walk is one of our favourites.
On private property in a seldom visited area of the Tararua foothills that offers two walks. Both stop at the Trotternish Shed which is located beside a hidden large pond on a remote corner of the farm for a cup of tea / coffee and a snack.

The Valley Walk follows a gentle 4WD track up a steep sided valley to the shed.
Depending on the weather the return walk can go down the opposite side of the valley via Side by Side vehicle tracks.
Walking time is about 60 minutes including an approximately 15 minute stop at the shed.

The UP and Over walk is for the fitter walkers.
It climbs steeply up Side by Side tracks up to the ridgeline. There is a lookout point with unique views into the Tararuas. A 10 minute stop to catch your breath then the track descends quickly down into the valley and around to the shed for drinks and snacks.
We return to the carpark via the Valley walk 4WD track.
Around a 2 hour walk (including stops).
Walkers on this walk are recommended to carry a small backpack with water and extra clothing.

name: Crochet - Christmas Special!
venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
long_description:
In this half day crochet special, you will get the patterns to make stars, and icicles, mini wreaths, a mini Christmas jumper, Christmas tree and gifts bunting and a cute mini Christmas hat. Please bring some 4 or 8 ply smooth yarn and a crochet hook - see full description for suitable types of yarn.

Description

Join Monique in this half-day crochet workshop where you will learn how to crochet a range of little projects suitable for the holiday season. Choose from stars, icicles, mini wreaths and Christmas jumpers, Christmas trees and a mini Santa hat! There will be a booklet of patterns for you to take home, to enable you to complete in your own time the projects that you didn’t have time to make during the workshop.

You will also learn how to crochet and decorate Christmas baubles! While you might not finish all the patterns this day, the aim is to have a go at making as many as possible!

You will need to know some basic crochet stitches such as single and double crochet. You’ll also need to have some understanding of how to read a pattern and work with diagrams, as taught in the beginners’ crochet course.

Please bring yarn that you enjoy working with (cotton, acrylic or wool, 4ply or 8 ply) in a variety of colours (red, white and green, a neutral colour for the mouse, and glittery yarns are all good options for the Christmas projects) and a matching crochet hook. You’ll also need a pair of scissors and a darning needle.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

venue: The Thistle Inn, 3 Mulgrave St, Thorndon, Wellington
long_description:
Celebrate Halloween with an evening of local ghost stories at the historic (and reputedly haunted!) Thistle Inn.

Join historian and lover of all things spooky Amanda McVitty on this fun, enlightening journey into Wellington’s uncanny past. Enjoy drinks and nibbles while you listen to chilling tales of phantom coaches, poltergeists, haunted houses, and eerie encounters on the night-time streets of colonial Wellington.

Includes a glass of bubbly and nibbles on arrival.

About your host:

Amanda McVitty is a professional historian and writer based in Wellington. She holds a doctorate in medieval European history and taught at Massey University for a decade, before turning to researching and writing about the history of Aotearoa New Zealand. She’s currently writing a book about ghosts and haunting in colonial New Zealand.

This event is part of the Wellington Heritage Festival 2026.

venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
long_description:
THEME: Resetting yourself

Guided drawings to reset your wants and needs

Join us for a DRAW IT OUT drawing for wellness workshop. Practice the ‘art’ of drawing and writing for wellness. This 1.5 hour workshop takes you through guided cues (similar to meditation or journaling) to draw out where you are at, draw out how you are feeling, and draw out your own inner guidance.

We all have the resources within to guide us, this workshop creates the space to access this by using a modality called Interactive Drawing Therapy. Facilitated by Lara Phillips, this is not therapy rather drawing for wellness; a guided workshop to build one’s relationship with oneself, to strengthen self-reflection and self-care.

No drawing skills required, this is more mark making not art making.

id: NZTrio: Reverie-Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, 65 Victoria St, Wellington-Event Finder
name: NZTrio: Reverie
venue: Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, 65 Victoria St, Wellington
long_description:
Reverie opens with a mesmerizing, atmospheric work that gently rocks between dream and reality - Hanna Kulenty’s A Cradle Song. The shimmering textures of Adam Schoenberg’s Las Estrellas unfold into a celestial dance, while Leonard Bernstein’s youthful Piano Trio provides a taste of his early brilliance and quirky personality, foreshadowing the irrepressible energy of his later Broadway compositions. A new NZTrio/SOUNZ Tarling Trust commission, Icarus on Titan from Karlo Margetič, situates the trio as explorers on an alien world, before entering a state of Romantic fervour with Schumann’s Piano Trio No. 3, which is brimming with lyrical expression.

Described as a “national treasure” (NZ Herald), NZTrio He Taonga Wairere is renowned for its eclectic repertoire, outstanding talent and warm kiwi stage presence. Bringing together three incredibly accomplished artists: Amalia Hall (violin), Matthias Balzat (cello) & Somi Kim (piano), every NZTrio performance powerfully reaffirms the importance and cathartic nature of a live musical experience in today’s digital world.

Hanna Kulenty - A Cradle Song
Adam Schoenberg - Las Estrellas
Leonard Bernstein - Piano Trio
Karlo Margetić (NZ) - Icarus on Titan (2026 NZTrio / SOUNZ Tarling Trust Commission)
Robert Schumann - Piano Trio No. 3 in g minor

Duration approx 105mins including 20min interval

name: Cooking Classes
venue: Sheila's Indian Kitchen, Ashton Fitchett Dr, Wellington
long_description:
Authentic Indian cooking classes in Wellington with panaromic views over Wellington Harbour.

In each class, you will learn 4-5 recipes like: potato stuff roti, roasted eggplant curry, wholemeal, roti, naan; shahi paneer; dhal, samosa; palak paneer; gourmet chickpeas; vegetable korma; gulab jamun; kheer; mango lassi; masala chai, and many more...

The classes start at 6 pm or 10:30 am on weekends and weekdays with a 2-hour session followed by a dinner or lunch afterwards. The ingredients, copies of recipes, organic karma drink will be provided with a full course meal in a banquet setting. Custom made classes available for gluten free, dairy free and any other food intolerance and dietary requirements.The ingredients, recipes, complimentary organic karma drinks will be provided with a full course meal.

There are 2 to 8 people in each class in purpose built cooking studio. Also a private cooking classes available.

The menu for the class can be:

1) Spicy potato stuffed paratha and roti, rajasthani tomato relish, aalu matter or spicy peas- potato curry, roasted cumin yogurt raita and fresh mint- coriander chutney.

2) Shahi Paneer (cottage cheese cubes with spices and rich tomato-cashew gravy), garlic coriander naan, cumin jeera basmati rice and sweet fragrant rice pudding with cardamom. Also I will teach how to make fresh paneer.

3) Roasted eggplant curry, plain whole wheat chapatti or roti, jeera aaloo or potato curry, Tuar dahl (split yellow lentil) and Basmati rice with homemade pickle.

4) Palak paneer (creamy spinach curry with cubes of paneer), jeera rice (basmati rice with fragrant spices, panjabi chhole or spicy chickpeas curry and mango lassi. Also fresh paneer making.

5) Khadi (chickpeas fritters in yogurt and chickpeas flour soupy gravy), Aloo-Gobhi (cauliflower and potato curry),  savoury wraps with herbs and spices, fresh pickle and basmati rice.

The total cost is $130 per person, this includes ingredient cost. (As an alternative we also sell cooking class gift vouchers.The food options are unlimited and the class provides fresh and best ingredients)
For booking a class please contact indiancooking@xtra.co.nz

Just bring your taste buds! and Enjoy!!

id: Mātātupu Mātauranga: Future Thinkers-Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, 55 Cable St, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Mātātupu Mātauranga: Future Thinkers
venue: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, 55 Cable St, Wellington
long_description:
Mātātupu Mātauranga: Future Thinkers celebrates rangatahi (15–24yo) and their unique perspective on the world. Get involved with te taiao-related creative workshops, tours, and activities, and then round out the day with a wānanga on how rangatahi envision a climate-focused future.

Painting the Future
10.00am–1.00pm, The Promenade
Dream up a sustainable future – bring it to life through painting and drawing. Work collaboratively with others to create a collaged vision of a climate-focused future.

Print Planting
10.00am–1.00pm, Signs of a Nation
Join illustrator Tayla Hartemink (Tūhoe, Te Arawa) to learn about stamp printing and plants growing in your backyard. Bring something from home to stamp or get creative on paper and fabric.

Fa‘atupu: Giving new life to old words (registration required)
10:30–12.00pm, Hīnātore
Join Mauatua Fa‘ara-Reynolds for this writing workshop inspired by the propagation of the aute plants across the Pacific. Participants are invited to bring excerpts of their own writing, or words from others, and use them as seeds for generating new work.
Registrations required for this session: https://events.humanitix.com/fa-atupu-giving-new-life-to-old-words

Beyond Be-leaf: Plant Stories in Bush City
10.30–11.30am and 12.00–1.00pm, Bush City Kiosk
What can plants teach us? What stories lie beyond the leaf? Join Curator Botany Leon Perrie for a tour of Bush City and work together to identify plants that are growing in our backyard during kōanga.

Holding Light: Slow Looking Tour
10.30–11.30am, 12.00–1.00pm, Slow Burn | Ahi Tāmau
Join slow looking tauira in a tour of Slow Burn | Ahi Tāmau – venture deep into photographic works made by rangatahi artists to discover how light illuminates stories.

Climate Wānanga
1.00–2.00pm, Rongomaraeroa, the marae
Indigenous rangatahi are the rākaugloss holding up the sky. This wānanga brings together young leaders in climate education and environmental justice to share how their work brings us closer to a climate-focused future.

Guest speakers announced very soon.

id: Watercolour Landforms Painting Workshop-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Watercolour Landforms Painting Workshop
venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
long_description:
Dramatic landforms catch my eye and intrigue me and I desire to portray the forms in watercolour. Learn how to capture the light on the ridges and define the shadows in the valleys. I share my approach with my students by sharing the colours to use, how to start and how to proceed step by step. In this two-day workshop you will use the core techniques of watercolour to paint landforms. We will refresh our knowledge of washes and edges, then use them to create beautiful landscape paintings.

Charlotte will demonstrate her watercolour painting techniques using bright colours and good quality materials She uses an overhead camera projected onto a 42-inch TV for easy step by step instruction. .The course will cover strategies for building a composition, delicate washes and how to achieve spatial depth in landscapes.

Please note this is not a beginners class and you must bring your own materials. This workshop is for intermediate to advanced watercolour painters.

What to bring -

Paints: We will use the basics: Raw Sienna, Alizarin, Cobalt as primary colours, Burnt Sienna, Ultramarine, Viridian, Quinacridone Gold and Indigo - but bring all the other colours and brands you regularly use.

Paper: Bring 4 quarter sheets - quality 100% cotton paper 300gsm watercolour paper for good results. Buy a full sheet (76 x 56 cm) and tear into four quarter sheets for the four paintings we will make over the weekend, or good quality A3 pad is OK. Cold pressed, hot pressed or rough - I recommend Arches, Saunders Waterford. Bring extra paper for the exercises.

Brushes: Bring your favourite brushes including a large mop and Hake for wetting large areas quickly. There will brushes for purchase.

Bring all the usual paraphernalia for painting including water container, masking tape, pencil, ruler, rubber, cloth, tissues, spray bottle, hair dryer. I usually work flat on the table or prop up the board.

One hour lunch each day - bring a packed lunch to enjoy in our historic house or explore the local Te Aro cafes. Coffee and tea provided at lunch.

id: Celtic Caim at Greytown Upclose & Personal-Cobblestones Heritage Village, 169 Main Street, Greytown-Event Finder
name: Celtic Caim at Greytown Upclose & Personal
venue: Cobblestones Heritage Village, 169 Main Street, Greytown
long_description:
A very special concert at Cobblestones Museum. We will welcome Celtic Caim - Heather Innes and Pauline Vallance for one concert only. Celtic Caim is a Celtic blessing and Pauline is in NZ for a short time only so we are fortunate for have secured one concert with her. Pauline and Heather, began singing together in 2014 and became Celtic Caim for tours of Canada, Australia and New Zealand in 2017, 2018 and 2019. Celtic Caim concerts have been described as "hauntingly beautiful harmony singing” and include an eclectic mix of Celtic songs, songs written by various songwriters, including Pauline & Heather plus jigs and reels on flute and bodhrán to get your feet tapping!

Pauline Vallance (vocals, clasarch, flute) is a singer/songwriter from Ayrshire, Scotland. She loves singing traditional songs from Ireland and Scotland plus her own songs, and she has a highly developed sense of the absurd! Pauline performs regularly throughout the UK. Her live performances have been described as "delightful and convivial on so many levels". Pauline’s latest album “The World's a Gift”, funded by Creative Scotland, was nominated for Scottish Album of the Year. She has written theatre shows about poets Robert Burns and Robert Tannahill as well as Echoes of the Land, which deals with having to leave your homeland and the longing for home.

Heather Innes (vocals, bodhrán) After living and singing in Australia and UK, Heather moved to New Zealand in 2022 and now lives locally in the Wairarapa. Heather sings from her heart, powerful ballads to gentle lullaby, with a timely sense of humour in between.

She began singing professionally in 1990 after recording her first album All’s Fair in Love and War at Spring Records, Rostrevor, Northern Ireland in 1989. Over the years she’s toured solo, and in bands and duos, in the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Thailand, Germany, Denmark, Ireland, Canada and USA. As well as recording 16 albums with various bands and duos, Heather has five solo CDs.

Bookings to 02102361951 by txt and $30 cash (no EFTPOS) on the door or through Eventfinda.

name: Reb Fountain - Water for Gasoline Tour
venue: Meow Nui, 92 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, Wellington
long_description:
Reb Fountains new album Water For Gasoline delivers another striking body of work from one of New Zealand's most acclaimed contemporary artists, a record that confronts the challenges of our times while searching for light, beauty and connection amongst the noise.
The same artistic instinct and collective spirit that shapes Water for Gasoline has long defined Reb Fountain’s live performances, with her live band taking her recordings to the next level. In celebration of her new work, Reb brings an enhanced band line up to audiences across Aotearoa and Australia this October, featuring Dianne Swann and James Duncan alongside bandmates Dave Khan & Earl Robertson.

Joining Reb in Auckland is Otago artist Mads Harrop. After conquering the Student Radio Charts with her single ‘Contagious’ in 2020 Mads has continued to highlight themes of neurodiversity through her music. Her diagnosis of Tourette's syndrome in 2019 directly affects her songwriting with her track ‘Hiding in Colour’ written shortly after her diagnosis to help her through the challenge. Playing with her full band for both shows, Mads is a welcome addition to the tour.

name: InDuna - Favourite Colours (Release Show)
venue: Moon, 167 Riddiford Street, Wellington
long_description:
Following recent performances supporting internationally acclaimed Nigerian artist Seun Kuti & Egypt 80, Aotearoa-based South African artist InDuna is set to release his new single 'Favourite Colours' and celebrates with a special headline show at Moon, Newtown, Wellington on Friday 30th October 2026.

Blending Afro-pop, R&B and folk, InDuna's live show brings infectious rhythms and uplifting energy alongside the more personal stories behind the songs. 'Favourite Colours' is an atmospheric anthem about identity, healing and resilience, using colour as a metaphor for how anxiety, grief and disconnection can drain the vibrancy from life, and the journey back to yourself.

InDuna will be joined by a special guest support act, to be announced.

Wheelchair accessible, seated and standing available.

About InDuna
Artist and producer InDuna draws on his South African roots, raised between Johannesburg and Limpopo before moving to Aotearoa at fourteen. His sound fuses African rhythm with contemporary pop and electronic production. Highlights include the King's Trust Young Global Achiever Award (2024), his single 'Dreams' (Best Original Song, International Online Web Fest; Official NZ Hot Singles Chart; featured in 'Ink and Gold'), and his 2025 EP 'Go High' (#16, Official Top 20 Aotearoa Albums Chart). He's supported Seun Kuti & Egypt 80 and opened for JessB, Estère and Deva Mahal, with headline shows across Wellington and Auckland.

'Favourite Colours' is supported by New Zealand On Air.

List the key steps in setting up a hive
Describe how honey is extracted

Describe what needs to be done to manage Varoa and American Foul Brood
Construct kitset frames for a honey super
Open up and inspect a hive

long_description:

Everyone will leave with a beautifully finished, solid silver bangle with their own preferred texture. You can finish your copper bangle too, and leave with a set!

We’ll begin by learning the basic technique on your copper, where you’ll practice creating textures using little hammers. Once you’re confident you’ll move on to your main project: a length of round solid silver wire, to be turned into a slender bangle crafted entirely by you from start to finish. Along the way, you’ll learn essential jewellery making skills including measuring, texturing, soldering, shaping, and finishing.

Students are free to personalise their bangle with simple textures or leave it plain and give it a bright polish or a satin finish.

This workshop is a taster class: perfect for anyone seeking a fun, creative experience with a beautiful result, or for those looking to dip their toes into jewellery making and build foundational skills.

Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio if you wish to make more.

id: 2026 EMPA Conference New Zealand-Tākina Wellington Convention Centre, 50 Cable Street, Te Aro, Wellington, Wellington-Event Finder
name: 2026 EMPA Conference New Zealand
venue: Tākina Wellington Convention Centre, 50 Cable Street, Te Aro, Wellington, Wellington
long_description:
Hosted once again at Wellington’s Te Papa on Thursday 5th and Friday 6th November, the EMPA NZ conference committee has pulled together another outstanding programme of presentations, workshops and networking.

One of this year’s international speakers will be Mark Ryan, who is the General Manager of Disaster and Emergency Management and Local Disaster Coordinator for the City of Gold Coast and will be sharing lessons learned from Cyclone Alfred. Mark’s presentation was one of the highlights of the recent EMPA conference in Brisbane and we’re delighted he has accepted our invitation to pop over the Tasman in November.

Lucy Easthope is an international expert and adviser on emergency planning and disaster recovery, who will be speaking about her experiences from mass casualty events. She is a visiting professor in mass fatalities and pandemics at the Centre for Death and Society at the University of Bath and also a researcher at the Joint Centre for Disaster Research at Massey University here in New Zealand.

Closer to home, Judge Anna Tutton will be providing us with an introduction to coronial inquests following an emergency and we’ll also hear from some of those emergency communicators who have been called to give evidence.

Jo Lynskey, Emergency Management Officer and Recovery Manager for the Western Bay of Plenty District Council, will also be presenting a case study on the recovery from recent landslides and flooding in the region.

The full programme can be found at https://www.empa.org.au/

The conference also features the finalists from our annual Awards for Excellence in Emergency Communication with six different categories covering all aspects of communicating in emergency situations.

We look forward to celebrating the very best projects from the last 12 months in style at our gala awards dinner on the Thursday evening.

id: Mini Masterpieces - Enamels Short Course-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
name: Mini Masterpieces - Enamels Short Course
venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
long_description:
Love pattern, colour and beautiful little things? You don't need to be an artist to create your own miniature masterpiece.

Glass enamels have been used on metal for centuries to create tiny works of art — from portraits and religious icons to royal emblems and intricate decorative pieces. Now it's your turn to discover this wonderfully tactile process.

Over two three-hour sessions, expert tutor Sarah Brock will guide you through creating a miniature artwork on a pre-cut metal shape. You'll start by preparing your metal and building a beautiful enamel background, then choose from a selection of patterns to trace and decals to create your design. No drawing skills are required — Sarah will help you find a design you love and show you how to make it work beautifully on your piece.

From there, you'll build up layers of coloured transparent enamels, ceramic pencil details and special effects, firing your piece between layers in the kiln. With each firing, the colours and textures develop, creating depth, richness and that gorgeous glassy enamel finish.
Your finished piece could become a special piece of jewellery, a keepsake ornament, or a tiny artwork to display in your home.

Perfect for anyone who loves colour, pattern, illustration and design, whether you're completely new to enamelling or simply looking for a new creative medium to explore. Come with an idea, or come with absolutely no idea — Sarah will help you turn it into something beautiful.
All class materials supplied.

Since the 1980’s tourism has exploded in Thailand and this nation’s cuisine has become one of the five most popular food types globally. Come and learn how to prepare and cook some delicious authentic Thai dishes.

Thai cuisine and cooking has a key secret - the secret is that authentic Thai food balances key flavour elements. id: Eigenface - Album Release Tour-Vogelmorn Bowling Club, 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Eigenface - Album Release Tour
venue: Vogelmorn Bowling Club, 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington
long_description:
Eigenface are heading out on a tour around Aotearoa to celebrate the release of their debut album, with support from Michaela Tempers.

Eigenface is a New Zealand/New York trio that blend folk intimacy, dream-punk atmospheres and electronic experimentation. Their songs move between comfort and unease, pairing bright melodies with dissonance, layered vocal harmonies and richly textured arrangements.
"Eigenface have developed a softly charming style that finds beauty in uncertainty. Their sound finds comparison with US indie rock acts Loma and Son Lux (both also trios), but for many the apparent connection will be to the stellar likes of Radiohead and Portishead." (Richard Thorne, NZ Musician). "It's the type of thing you can listen to over and over again" (Chi-Chi Attard, Happy Mag - Australia). "Dynamic, intriguing and addictive: it pulls you in and refuses to let go" (Oliver Zurita of Expansión Radial - Spain).

The band comprises Penelope Esplin (French for Rabbits, Lake South, Grawlixes) on synth and vocals, Elliot Vaughan (CNZ/NZSM Composer in Residence 2024, Moth Quartet, RNZ Concert Presenter) on bass and vocals, and Logan Valentine (Moon Lander) on electric guitar and vocals. For these shows, Penelope and Elliot will be travelling as a duo, bringing Eigenface into a more intimate live setting. The group formed from an impromptu challenge to write and perform on one another's work, the result became a cohesive set of songs, resulting in Eigenface's self-titled debut album.

Released on Home Alone Records, Eigenface arrives on October 2, 2026. Recorded and mixed by Vaughan and mastered by Harris Newman (Wolf Parade, Buck Meek, Godspeed You! Black Emperor), the album features Vaughan's lush string arrangements throughout. Across its songs, the band explores memory, place, relationships and the tension between beauty and discomfort through expansive arrangements, electronic textures and intimate storytelling.

Eigenface’s debut single, House by the Sea, reached #1 on RDU (Christchurch), #4 on Radio1 (Dunedin) and #2 on the Student Radio Network Charts. Their second single, Slow Exposure, reached #1 on RDU, #3 on Radioactive (Wellington) and #2 on the SRN Charts. Their third single, Twizel, reached #1 on RDU and #1 on the SRN Charts. They've now been nominated for the SRN People's Choice Awards 2026. Eigenface have appeared at Day in the Bay, The Performance Arcade and Newtown Festival, and shared stages with Lake South, Julian Temple and The Broken Heartbreakers.

Michaela Tempers is a writer and musician based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara, Aotearoa. Tempers singing voice has been described as “a rare warbling instrument that will leave you grasping for comparisons” (Tony Stamp, RNZ). “Her voice and musical vision establish her as a striking new presence in our ever growing and evolving folk music landscape – honest, rich, insightful.” (Tim Gruar, Muzic.NZ).

Tempers’ debut EP, recorded alongside producers Brooke Singer (French for Rabbits) and Chris Armour (Miles Calder, Louis TM ), is brimming with “sincerity leavened by wit and uniquely dynamic constructs” (Richard Thorne, NZ Musician). Tempers will be joined by Dayle Jellyman (organ) for the North Island shows, and Chris Armour (guitar) for the Wellington show. She has opened for Creedence Clearwater Revival, Holly Arrowsmith, Jed Parsons, Irish folk band Boega, as well as Australian folk artists Boy & Bear.

Saturday 3rd October – Pearl Diver, Dunedin
Friday 6th November – Vogelmorn, Wellington
Saturday 7th November – Porridge Watson, Whanganui
Thursday 12th November – Big Fan, Auckland

id: Therapeutic Gong Bath with Hammocks!-The Yoga Studio, 6/149 Karori Rd, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Therapeutic Gong Bath with Hammocks!
venue: The Yoga Studio, 6/149 Karori Rd, Wellington
long_description:
Join Nick for his last therapeutic Gong Bath with your choice of hammock or floor seat, to soak in the vibrations and beautiful droning sounds of three medium-large Paiste 'Planet' gongs, Tibetan 'full moon' bowls, and medium sized sound therapy instruments.

The science behind these gongs baths are: the rich harmonics of the gongs invite your body and mind to rest into deeper brainwave states, and the drones invite the nervous system to relax because the long continuous sounds say 'things are moving slowly, this is safe'. The sounds themselves are like some kind of rich, harmonic, cosmic electronic music yet primal and organic. Nick uses three medium-large Paiste 'Planet' gongs, which are tuned to a fundamental pitch, and were developed specifically for sound therapy compared to some other gongs.

Nick has been producing and playing with music since his earliest teens, having graduated from The New Zealand School of Music, and The University of Auckland in Psychology with over 4 years of work experience in experiential therapies, combining musical and therapeutic worlds with events like these throughout Wellington and the lower North Island for the past 2.5+ years. He uses Somatic Psychology informed grounding practices at the beginning and end of the session

The Yoga Studio has ample free parking and easy access via Bus Route 2 at the Marsden Village stop. The studio is up the blue wooden staircase which you can see when you're in the carpark in the Masden Village. Please arrive 5ish minutes early, so we can start at 6pm for the grounding introduction.

Please bring along anything that'll help you feel more comfortable (blankets, pillows, and bolsters come with your ticket, but you can bring along eye masks, earplugs etc if you need that).

If you live with any of these, please talk to your Doctor first, to make sure the event will be suitable:
-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)

If you're trying to decide between the hammock or floor ticket, the hammock is better for slightly shorter people (under 5"8), while the floor is good for people who like to stretch out more.

See you there!

id: Jesus Christ Superstar-St James Theatre, 77-87 Courtenay Place, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Jesus Christ Superstar
venue: St James Theatre, 77-87 Courtenay Place, Wellington
long_description:
Following acclaimed and sold-out runs in London as well as an extensive tour of North America, the UK, and Australia, the Olivier Award-winning reimagined production of Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber celebrated musical JESUS CHRIST SUPERSTAR will play in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch this October through to December, as part of a major international tour.

Featuring lyrics and music by Emmy, GRAMMY, Oscar, and Tony winners Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber, this production was reimagined by London’s Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre, where it originated, and is helmed by director Timothy Sheader and choreographer Drew McOnie. Completing the creative team is design by Tom Scutt, lighting design by Lee Curran, sound design by Nick Lidster, and music supervision by Tom Deering.

A global phenomenon that has wowed audiences for decades, JESUS CHRIST SUPERSTAR is a timeless work that explores the biblical portrayal of the extraordinary events that led to the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ as seen through the eyes of his betrayer, Judas Iscariot. The story, told entirely through song, explores the personal relationships and struggles among Jesus, Judas, Mary Magdalene, Jesus’ disciples, his followers and the Roman Empire. Originally released as a concept album, the iconic 1970s rock score contains such well-known numbers as ‘Superstar’, ‘I Don’t Know How to Love Him’, and ‘Gethsemane’.

name: Sunday Morning Jewellery-making In 4 Weeks - Mixed Level
venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
long_description:
Spend your Sunday mornings immersed in creativity, learning the timeless craft of jewellery-making in our warm, welcoming studio.

It runs from Sun 1 November for 4 weeks till Sun 22 November, 10am-1pm.

This short course is the perfect introduction for complete beginners, guiding you step-by-step through the essential techniques used by jewellers. You’ll start by working in copper or brass, building confidence as you learn to cut, heat, shape and texture metal. From there, you can choose to move into silver and bring your ideas to life in more refined pieces.

A beautiful textured ring band is an ideal first project, but once you’ve mastered the basics, the possibilities really open up—create earrings, pendants, or small bespoke pieces that reflect your personal style. You’ll learn how to solder using a jeweller’s torch, refine your finishing techniques, and polish your work to a professional shine. It’s a hands-on, deeply satisfying process, and there’s nothing quite like wearing something you’ve made yourself.

These Sunday sessions are also perfect for returning students and more experienced makers who want dedicated studio time, guidance on more ambitious projects, and the chance to be part of a friendly, creative community.

Materials are purchased as you go, so you can tailor your projects to your budget and ideas. Beginners typically spend around $50–$70 on metals over the course.

This block is ideal for teens and young creatives aged 12 and up. Please note: anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

id: 2026 Pūkaha Wairarapa Garden Tour-South Wairarapa, State Highway 2, Greytown-Event Finder
name: 2026 Pūkaha Wairarapa Garden Tour
venue: South Wairarapa, State Highway 2, Greytown
long_description:
Discover 12 spectacular gardens across South Wairarapa during one unforgettable spring weekend.

The 2026 Wairarapa Garden Tour invites you to explore a hand-picked collection of gardens located throughout Featherston, Martinborough, Greytown, Gladstone and surrounding areas. Over two days, you'll enjoy exclusive access to gardens that are rarely – if ever – open to the public, travelling at your own pace and creating your own itinerary.

This year's tour features an exceptional mix of historic country estates, contemporary landscapes and much-loved family gardens, each with its own character and appeal.
A major drawcard of this year's tour is the inclusion of two of Wairarapa's most significant heritage properties, both featuring on the Wairarapa Garden Tour for the first time. Fernside, a New Zealand Garden’s Trust listed property one of New Zealand's finest historic gardens, re-opened to visitors in 2025 after more than five years closed to the public, offering the rare opportunity to explore its magnificent grounds, heritage trees and rich history. Rototāwai, a remarkable country estate featuring beautiful gardens, a historic homestead and an on-site gallery, also makes its debut on the tour.

The Wairarapa Garden Tour celebrates gardens of every scale and style. Alongside the grand country estates, visitors will discover intimate town gardens, flourishing cottage plantings and thoughtfully designed contemporary spaces, each offering fresh ideas and inspiration. Many of the tour's most memorable moments come from seeing how passionate gardeners have transformed their own corner of Wairarapa.

The tour also features:
• The Market Fair – a vibrant garden setting showcasing local food, beverages, artisan goods and crafts, hosted at Fernside.
• Exclusive workshops hosted at selected gardens (details released in August).
• Opportunities to purchase plants, produce and small-batch products grown and made by garden owners.

The Wairarapa Garden Tour is a fundraising event for Pūkaha National Wildlife Centre. As Pūkaha's largest annual fundraiser, the tour helps support vital conservation work, including native species recovery, forest restoration, predator control and education programmes for local school children.

Gardens are open from 9.30am to 4.30pm each day.

Before starting your tour, you'll collect your wristband and printed map from designated collection points in Featherston, Martinborough or Greytown (locations to be announced).

Food trucks and coffee carts will be available at selected gardens, and visitors are welcome to bring a picnic and enjoy the beautiful surroundings.

Join us for a weekend celebrating exceptional gardens, passionate gardeners and the very best of South Wairarapa, while helping support the future of New Zealand's native wildlife.

Visitors should note:
• The tour goes ahead rain or shine.
• Pets are not permitted.
• Children are welcome but must be supervised at all times. Children 9 years and under do not require a ticket.
• Some gardens include natural hazards such as ponds and creeks.

Important visitor information:
Visitors enter all gardens at their own risk. While Pūkaha and participating garden owners take reasonable care to provide a safe environment, visitors are responsible for their own safety and personal belongings. Paths and garden surfaces may be uneven, slippery or contain natural hazards. Visitors should take care at all times and follow any instructions or signage provided by organisers, volunteers or garden owners. To the maximum extent permitted by law, Pūkaha and participating garden owners accept no liability for loss, damage or injury arising from a visitor's participation in the Wairarapa Garden Tour.

id: The Quickest Route to Salvation-BATS Theatre, 1 Kent Tce, Wellington-Event Finder
name: The Quickest Route to Salvation
venue: BATS Theatre, 1 Kent Tce, Wellington
long_description:
If you were faced with the inability to make decisions under pressure, would you outsource your decision-making to a collective consciousness of complete strangers?

When Sol, usually paralysed by everyday decision-making, enrolls in The Seer’s experimental neurological clinical trial, the audience is plugged in as the collective consciousness. They decide in real time how Sol navigates their setbacks. Enter Sol’s mind, where four distinct "Neurons" advocate for each of their conflicting responses to Sol’s dilemmas.

There are many unique mechanics to marvel at. The Branching Narrative gives the audience a unique chance to act as Sol's decision-makers, using voting panels to determine how the narrative progresses in real-time. The Original Score changes Dynamically depending on audience choices throughout the show, and the narrative branches into one of Four Different Endings. The branches feature Abstract Movement and Dance, giving the audience a unique perspective on their choices. There is no way to hear every song, and see every scene in just one night, each show is unique.

long_description:
Gate opens 7pm, Music starts 7.30pm.

Pip Payne, Richard Klein and Alan Norman are The Bon Temps Bros. PIP PAYNE, a regular player and founder of Capital Blues is back with another musical variation. Pip has had many artistic guises over the years which shows not only his versatility, bluesy vocals but also his depth of the music. He plays slide guitar, and plays regularly with Wayne Mason, Pops & The Tempests, the Caramellos, Dean Martinborough, Laura Collins Back Porch Band and more. Originally from Dorking, he now lives in Otaki Beach. RICHARD KLEIN is a high energy singing fiddler born in Orange, New Jersey. In his early teens he discovered folk and roots music through listening to the likes of Woody Guthrie, Pete Seeger and The New Lost City Ramblers. Travelling to Cape Breton Island in mid 1970s sparked the interest for Celtic music that later brought Richard to travel, live, work and busk extensively through Ireland and the British Isles. A chance meeting with a gang of Swedish fiddlers in Shetland in 1978 introduced another important influence in his fiddle style. But it was being properly introduced to Cajun music later that same year in France that had the most profound impact on his music. Resident in Wellington since 1997, Richard is best known for his collaboration with the Le Blanc Brothers Cajun Band (Melbourne) and the geographically challenged Kiwi Americana band. T-Bone. In 2023 he relinquished his American citizenship. The accent, however, remains and you will find him to be a charming gentleman. AL NORMAN has been on the Wellington scene for decades. A multi-instrumentalist with a great feel for the groove, he plays with The Warratahs, Rag Poets, Bill Lake’s Slow Bake and Burgin, Kerr & Norman. He’s been part of a number of well-established groups including Smokeshop and The Laura Collins Band.

… A slide guitar, a fiddle, an accordion, and a snare drum. Together they make a big sound – and it’s all about the groove. Acoustically syncopated Cajun blues — hot Louisiana music.

Come along and enjoy this great gig in our special space, up close and personal.
These are private house concerts, not for profit, supporting our dedicated musicians. Visit www.hilltophouseconcerts.co.nz to reserve a seat. Suggested donation $30. Email confirmation will include address and details. Teas, Coffee and Snacks provided. You're welcome to bring anything you'd like to eat or drink. Parking available in the Coupon zones of Upland Rd & Glasgow St free after 6pm weekdays, and free all through the weekends. The Wilson Carpark at the top of the Cable Car charges 24/7.

long_description:
Grab a spot on our couch and enjoy the noise at The Racket Lounge - a chill classical music series showcasing up-and-coming Pōneke musicians.

If you’ve never been to a classical concert before, or if you have and now you want to see talented emerging musicians experimenting and playing what they want to play, then The Racket Lounge is for you. Over the past two seasons we’ve seen classical covers, jazz ensembles, video game soundtracks, original compositions, loop pedals, poetry and much more. Our 2026 season is shaping up to be just as epic, plus with your tickets starting at just $5 you can afford to take a chance on something new.

Each concert will feature a different line up of musicians and genres, to be announced a week before each session. If you’re a musician looking to perform at The Racket Lounge, then head to the New Zealand String Quartet’s website to see how to apply.

We are so ready to be entranced by Wellington’s top up-and-coming talent at our second Racket Lounge session, “Moonlight Dash”. Filled with cozy, romantic grooves from 1836 to 2026, these stunningly talented up and comers are set to dazzle us whether the moon is shining bright or we’re dashing through the rain. Sip your drink through soulful, acoustic moments and tap your toes to inspiringly energetic rhythms. Come inside and soak up the chillest of vibes (rather than Wellington’s very chilly rain) at The Racket Lounge: Moonlight Dash. 

The Racket Lounge is created and presented by the New Zealand String Quartet Trust - Te Rōpū Tūrū o Aotearoa, New Zealand’s longest-running professional string quartet. With support from Wellington City Council.

Our ticket prices range from $5 to $100, so just pick the ticket price you feel like paying. At The Racket Lounge, we believe everyone should have access to high-quality but affordable art. If you're a bit strapped for cash right now, but still want a good night out, no worries! Just book yourself a $5 ticket! If you can afford to pay a little more and want to do some good for your community, then pick one of our higher ticket prices and rest assured that your dollars are going towards funding great, accessible art in your city.

All proceeds from ticket sales will go directly into presenting the next Racket Lounge, including paying musicians and artists, hiring instruments and marketing costs. Plus, by choosing a higher price point, you're ensuring that we're able to continue to offer tickets at a lower price point for those who need it.

PLEASE NOTE: Bedlam & Squalor is a licensed venue, so under 18s must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. Everyone must bring ID.

long_description:
Step inside the World of WearableArt® and hear from the people at the heart of the spectacle.

WOW: Meet the Makers is an inspiring evening of stories, creativity and insight, featuring some of the region's most accomplished WOW designers. Hear from 2026 Supreme WOW Award winner Kayla Christensen as she shares her journey to the top of the world's premier wearable art competition, alongside fellow Kāpiti designer Rebecca Bond, whose imaginative work has earned recognition on the WOW stage. Guests will also enjoy reflections from legendary WOW designer Fifi Colston, a 30-time entrant and multi-award winner whose extraordinary body of work has helped shape the competition's history.

id: This Is Grief: On the Road-Paraparaumu Public Library, 9 Iver Trask Place, Paraparaumu-Event Finder
name: This Is Grief: On the Road
venue: Paraparaumu Public Library, 9 Iver Trask Place, Paraparaumu
long_description:
Grief is part of being human, but we still struggle to talk about it.

This Is Grief: On the Road is a free community event bringing honest conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them into communities across Aotearoa.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O'Connor for a relaxed, human conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the clichés, timelines and expectations we so often place around it. Kirsten will share from her own experience of grief and from her work writing and talking about loss, before opening the space for conversation and connection.

You don't need to have the right words. You don't need to share anything you don't want to. This is a space for anyone living with loss, or anyone who wants to better understand and support someone who is.

Come along, listen, talk if you'd like to, and be part of a conversation we don't have nearly often enough.

This is a free community event. Registration is recommended as places may be limited.

long_description:

Join Chris Cochran at Waiorongomai Station to explore what these remarkable buildings reveal about our region’s history.

long_description:

Join us for a 60 to 75-minute guided walk exploring the fascinating world of plants and the stories they tell. From ancient survivors and remarkable adaptations to the clues plants give us about changing landscapes, you'll discover how foliage can reveal both the history of our planet and the natural world around us.

As we make our way downhill through Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā, we'll stop to admire a diverse range of trees, shrubs, and groundcovers while uncovering the science, history, and surprising tales hidden among the leaves.

This is part of the regular walks run by the Friends of the Wellington Botanic Garden. They run throughout the year with a different topic every time.

Join the Friends for only $30 a year and all the walks will be free, as well as other great benefits.

id: Glass Mosaic Day-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
name: Glass Mosaic Day
venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
long_description:
This day class will cover making small, interior mosaics on wood bases using stunning brightly coloured glass.

Small mosaics are really quick and simple to make - and can create a real design punch with colourful glass pieces and a range of really nice backing shapes and frames. This is a great place to start if you want to get into Mosaics, and work up to glass-on-glass, exterior mosaics or three-D mosaics.

You can choose from either :
A micro set of mosaics - suitable for tiny wall-sets or bespoke heirloom ornaments
Box framed bases, ready to hang.
A range of simple cut-out shapes that could be hung on a wall or mounted on doors.

The class covers:
Preparing your bases and materials, choosing adhesives that suit interior projects.
Planning and choosing simple designs to make your mosaics really pop
How to snip your glass down into tiny pieces if needed (most pieces are already cut for you)
Working with adhesives, tips and tricks with tools.

Finally we will cover grouting and finishing your mosaics - due to the time it takes for grout to fully cure, some cleanup and final sealing coats will need to be done later on at home, you’ll be given clear instructions and the sealant to apply at the end of the class.

We can also look at options for hanging and mounting - we have some simple fittings for you to choose from.

Some students may finish in time to grout your pieces - seeing these pieces are SO small, they are often dry enough for grouting. Or you can take your grout away to do at home, or leave with us to grout for you and collect in a few days. (There’s a small fee attached to that part.)

This is a warm, friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and those who want to start working with hand-cut glass terraria.

All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.
Materials for the main class projects are supplied as part of your course fee.

Young makers aged 12 and up are welcome to join the class, as long as they are able to work safely with sharp glass and tools.

Anyone under the age of 16 must attend with an enrolled parent or caregiver who is there to support them and participate alongside them.

id: Jewellery-making On Thursdays, 8-week Block, Level 2+-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Jewellery-making On Thursdays, 8-week Block, Level 2+
venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
long_description:
Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

The course starts on Thursday 29 October and runs for 8 weeks till Thursday 17 December, 5.30pm-8pm.

This class is designed for students who already have some skills and are ready to develop their craftsmanship in a lively, warm, and supportive environment. Guided by our highly skilled tutors, you’ll build confidence, refine your techniques, and gain the satisfaction of making jewellery that reflects your personal style.

If you’re brand new to jewellery making, we recommend beginning with our Tuesday Evening 8-Week Beginners’ Block, which gives a solid foundation in essential techniques before moving on to this class.

At Level 2, the focus is on precision and technique. Students explore the art of chain making, a classic jewellery making project that develops fine soldering skills and accuracy in construction. This project is an excellent way to build confidence with the torch and create a piece of jewellery that is both functional and beautiful. The finished chain can become a pendant, bracelet, or necklace, or you may choose to adapt it into a design of your own.

At Level 3 and above, the emphasis shifts toward creativity and design development. Students at this stage are encouraged to take on more complex projects, experiment with new and challenging techniques, and bring their own design ideas to life. With the guidance of our skilled and supportive tutors, you’ll learn how to push your skills further, problem-solve during the making process, and refine your eye for detail and design.

Evening classes are not just about the technical side of jewellery making - they are also a chance to slow down, enjoy the process, and be part of a creative community. Many students return term after term, finding the rhythm of regular making both mindful and rewarding.

Please note: this class does not include a materials allowance, giving you the flexibility to choose your own metals, stones, or other materials. You only pay for what you use, making it easier to customise your projects and work at your own pace.

Our booking system asks for full payment at the time of registration (via credit card, PayPal, or AfterPay). If you don’t have access to these options or would like to pay in instalments, please email us and we’ll happily arrange an alternative.

name: Cheesemaking - Brie And Queso Fresco
venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
long_description:
During this intensely practical, hands-on workshop, you will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Double Cream ‘NZ style’ Brie. You will also be shown how to make Queso Fresco cheese which you will get to sample afterwards. All ingredients included in course fee.

The ultimate class in practical cheese making! Learn all you need to know to replicate making NZ style Brie and Queso Fresco at home. You will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Brie. Then, while the Brie is ripening and setting (don't worry, all terminology will be explained!), we will make Queso Fresco together.

All ingredients are provided as are recipes and detailed handouts to take away with you. Bring an apron, a dishcloth, 3 or 4 tea towels, a pen to take notes and a 2 litre container and plastic re-sealable food bags to take your cheese home.

During the workshop, the following topics will also be covered: Milk and where to source it, hygiene and sanitation, equipment required and the origins of the cheeses you are about to make. You will also receive comprehensive instruction on how to mature your Brie cheese over the next few weeks.

A small break will be provided and you will have the opportunity to purchase equipment and cheesemaking ingredients after the workshop should you wish to replicate the experience at home.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:

Make Brie and Queso Fresco
Recall the best milk to use and where to source it from
Name and identify what equipment and ingredients you need to make Brie and Queso Fresco
