id: Botanical Insights Talk - Electrical Secrets of Plants and Fungi-Wellington Botanic Garden, 101 Glenmore St, Kelburn, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Botanical Insights Talk - Electrical Secrets of Plants and Fungi
venue: Wellington Botanic Garden, 101 Glenmore St, Kelburn, Wellington
long_description:
This one-hour talk will reveal how plants’ electrical signalling system enables them to sense and respond rapidly, within seconds, to their environment in order to coordinate growth, defence, photosynthesis and whole of-plant acclimation. It will outline the practical application of research findings. The talk will also examine electrical signalling in fungi and the actions of their mycelial networks in a range of biological and environmental settings. It will touch on the emergent field of fungal computers and probable applications

Located in the Seminar Room, Treehouse Visitor Centre and Shop, Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā.
Free of charge. You’re welcome to bring along your own ‘brown bag’ lunch to enjoy during the talk.

The speaker is Reg Harris, a volunteer guide [botany] at Wellington Botanic Garden.
Reg delivers botany lectures for diverse audiences, delving into plant interactions, adaptive radiation, tropisms, and more. As a dedicated volunteer guide at Wellington Botanic Garden (WBG), he pioneered collaborations between WBG and Victoria University, organising annual field labs for biology students.

id: Botanical Blues - Photographic cyanotype-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Botanical Blues - Photographic cyanotype
venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
long_description:
In this workshop, you’ll discover the beautiful 19th-century photographic process of the cyanotype (often called a blueprint), known for its striking Prussian blue tones. In its earliest form, the cyanotype was used to record botanical specimens.

During our workshop, you’ll collect plants or foliage from the garden (or bring your own) to create delicate contact prints, OR you can create stencils for abstract designs. We’ll coat Japanese rice paper with light-sensitive chemistry, expose your designs in the sunlight, and develop them. We’ll also cut a matt board for your favourite final print. You can bring your own papers to test printing on, but they must be non-coated (able to absorb chemistry) and wet-strength.

All materials included.

Thirty minute lunch - bring a packed lunch to have in our historic home or explore the local cafes in Te Aro.

name: Natural Textured Rings - Taster Class
venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
long_description:
Craft a beautiful, personalised ring - a perfect treat for yourself or a thoughtful gift for someone special! This three-hour taster class is designed for absolute beginners, though all skill levels are welcome to join the fun.

You will be guided step-by-step through the core techniques of silversmithing. You'll start by practicing basic texturing, cutting, and shaping with traditional jewellery tools using copper or brass. Once you’re comfortable, you'll move on to crafting your final piece in sterling silver.

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn to:
Measure your finger and cut the metal strip to the perfect length.
Create unique surface textures using a rolling mill, hammers, punches, and even natural elements like feathers or leaves. You can stamp names, dates, whatever you like.
Work safely with a jeweler's torch for heating and soldering the metal.
Finish your ring with sanding and polishing techniques.
By the end of the class, your beautiful, custom-made sterling silver ring will be ready to wear.

This is an ideal activity for individuals, groups of friends, or visitors to Ōtaki looking for a creative experience.

What's Included:
All practice materials (copper or brass).
A strip of sterling silver for your final ring.
All necessary consumables (sandpaper, solder, chemicals).
Use of all tools and equipment.

Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

long_description:
Tour this historically significant complex, built during World War I to provide recreation and hospitality for soldiers training at Featherston Military Camp.

Enjoy a fascinating guided tour of the historically significant Anzac Hall. The hall was first opened in 1916 as a recreation centre for the troops at the nearby Featherston military camp, with the families of the first European settlers donating the funds. The building was used as a hospital during the influenza epidemic of 1918-19. It is a Category One Historic Place. Be at the hall’s main entrance ten minutes before each tour starts.

Free event – all welcome!

They first meet a million years ago, in the eruption of a volcano.

The second time, it’s in a liquor store: Hinenuitepo is buying a lighter for Mahuika; Hinemoana is picking up drinks.

Before long, they become entangled in rituals of mortality— love, hot chips, a carved bone strap-on, multiple evictions and a new puppy—all while holding down their duties as Death and the Sea.

But there is a great sickness rising in them both. The other atua have begun to disappear, and their world is slowly dying. Somewhere, an insidious power waits.

As the story shifts between our two lovers, Puke weaves a modern puuraakau of desire, decay and decolonisation.

name: Ascent up Maunga Rangitūmau
venue: Te Rangi Lodge, 490 Bluff Rangitumau Rd, Masterton
long_description:
Ever wondered what that high hill is just north of Masterton with the aerials on it?
This is the impressive Rangitūmau Maunga - important in the story of Haunui-a-Nanaia, who long ago came this way after pursuing his runaway wife Wairaka down the west coast of Te Ika a Māui.

The group will meet and part at Te Rangi Lodge, and set off together up the hill.
The tramp is a steady, but not steep, uphill climb to the top where there are 360 degree views.

Local writer, researcher and storyteller Joe Potangaroa (Ngati Kahungunu, Rangitane, Tuhoe, English) will participate, and share his knowledge of tikanga, taiao and Wairarapa history linked to Maunga Rangitūmau.

The walk will take 2 - 2.5 hours and is suitable for fit walkers & trampers. The walk starts at 200m elevation and climbs to 604m elevation.
Please note access is through a working farm, please observe all health and safety instructions given on the day.

Koha accepted for the cuppa tea provided.

name: Stacking Rings - November Taster
venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
long_description:
Create your own ring stack from copper, brass, and sterling silver in this fun and rewarding jewellery workshop!

Guided by experienced and supportive tutors, you’ll be introduced to the fundamental skills of jewellery making while creating a small collection of rings to take home.

During this 3-hour class, you’ll learn how to measure your finger, cut metal to size, and add textures and patterns using hammers and punches. You’ll also be shown how to solder your rings with a jeweller’s torch, before finishing them with filing, sanding, and polishing techniques.

By the end of the session, you’ll have crafted a thick sterling silver ring and a stack of copper or brass rings, including two plain round wires to texture as you like, and a choice of decorative brass pearl wire or square wire.

This class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends, or visitors wanting a memorable creative experience. Many students find jewellery making a mindful activity, offering a chance to slow down, work with their hands, and enjoy the rhythm of making.

The class fee includes all materials and consumables, such as solder, sandpaper, and polishing materials. Extra silver and other metals will be available for purchase in the studio for those who would like to expand their collection or upgrade one of their brass or copper wires to a second silver one.

Children aged 12 and over are welcome. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

The always-brilliant Bill Nighy stars in 500 Miles, a life-affirming celebration of the human spirit that follows a broken family who are forced to come together when their two young boys run away from home. After hearing their parents fight, Finn (Roman Griffin Davis, Jojo Rabbit) and Charlie (Dexter Sol Ansell, breakout star of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms) sneak out of their house in Doncaster.

id: 2026 Wairarapa Garden Tour - Rototāwai Guided Tours with Ross Palmer-Rototāwai Gallery & Gardens, 808 Kahutara Road, Featherston-Event Finder
name: 2026 Wairarapa Garden Tour - Rototāwai Guided Tours with Ross Palmer
venue: Rototāwai Gallery & Gardens, 808 Kahutara Road, Featherston
long_description:
Guided Garden Tour with Ross Palmer

Discover the story behind Rotōtāwai on an exclusive one-hour guided tour led by acclaimed garden designer Ross Palmer, who helped reimagine the estate's remarkable gardens. As you explore the property, Ross will share the vision behind the design, the evolution of the landscape, and the careful balance of honouring the estate's heritage while creating a garden for the future.

Ross is the former owner and principal of London-based Kumara Studio, where he designed gardens across Europe, the USA, Australia, Aotearoa and Thailand. Now based in New Zealand, Ross specialises in the thoughtful restoration and evolution of significant country gardens, with Rotōtāwai and Welton House among the public gardens showcasing his work.

This is a rare opportunity to experience one of the Tour's most anticipated debut gardens through the eyes of its designer.

id: Concept to Completion: Masterclass with Charlie Faulks | Halloween 26-Aratoi Wairarapa Museum of Art and History, 12 Bruce St, Masterton-Event Finder
name: Concept to Completion: Masterclass with Charlie Faulks | Halloween 26
venue: Aratoi Wairarapa Museum of Art and History, 12 Bruce St, Masterton
long_description:
Concept to Completion: Masterclass with Charlie Faulks | Halloween 2026

How does a 19-year-old Screen Arts student get almost half a million dollars to make an animated zombie series set on a rural New Zealand farm?

That’s the story behind Bloke of the Apocalypse, and the starting point for an intimate masterclass with animator and filmmaker Charlie Faulks.

Charlie began developing Bloke of the Apocalypse while studying Screen Arts, making the first episodes independently before the project grew into a professionally funded animated series.

In this 90-minute masterclass, Charlie will take you behind the scenes of that journey, exploring how an idea develops, how early work can lead to bigger opportunities, finding collaborators, pitching and funding, animation and production, and what it takes to get a project through to completion.

There’ll be video excerpts and behind-the-scenes material, with plenty of time for questions and conversation.

This masterclass is for secondary students, aspiring filmmakers and animators, emerging creatives, writers, artists, storytellers, or anyone curious about how a screen idea becomes a finished project.

No previous filmmaking or animation experience is required.

Saturday 31 October 2026
1:00pm–2:30pm
Aratoi Wairarapa Museum of Art and History, Masterton

Adults $35
Secondary students $15

Places are strictly limited to 15.

This masterclass has been subsidised with grateful thanks to the Masterton District Creative Communities Scheme, helping make this professional development opportunity more accessible to the Wairarapa community.

Part of Halloween 2026 with The Story Studio.

id: Stained Glass Suncatcher Day-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
name: Stained Glass Suncatcher Day
venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
long_description:
Create gorgeous simple leadlight suncatchers with Lisa Sinclair.

A super fun day-class, ideal as a stand-alone experience, or as a day to get stuck into projects with your tutor at hand.

Beginners choose from a range of achievable patterns and choose their colour palette. They will learn to cut the glass, and prepare it before foiling and soldering each piece, creating a simple elegant colourful glass project.

The aim of this one day class is to leave with a completed small leadlight glass item.

Your materials for your beginner project are supplied as part of your course fee.

id: Korimako Trio-Martinborough Town Hall, 8 Texas Street, Martinborough-Event Finder
name: Korimako Trio
venue: Martinborough Town Hall, 8 Texas Street, Martinborough
long_description:
Korimako Trio
Helene Pohl, violin; Rolf Gjelsten, cello; Michael Endres, piano

The concert opens with Zemlinsky's Trio in D Minor, a late 19th century example of Viennese Romanticism, lyrical, dense and emotionally expressive. This is followed by Janacek’s Violin Sonata (for violin and piano) deeply dramatic with folk elements. A return to Romanticism with Chopin’s Introduction and Polonaise Brillante in C major, for cello and piano follows and the concert concludes with Haydn’s Piano trio in A major (Hob.XV), bright and witty, with plenty of classical charm. A beautifully varied journey through four distinct musical eras, balancing full trio textures with virtuoso duo highlights.

id: Derek vs Derek- British and Irish Film Festival-The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton-Event Finder
name: Derek vs Derek- British and Irish Film Festival
venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Thessaloniki International Documentary Festival -

What happens when your neighbour goes completely wild? Derek vs Derek is a funny, insightful and heartwarming documentary that charts the turbulent relationship between two farmers.

On a country road in Devon live two ideologically opposed neighbouring farmers- both called Derek. Derek Banbury believes in the intensive farming of his land, while Derek Gow is focused on creating a “rewilding” oasis for nature and wildlife on his land.

Shot over three years, Derek vs Derek wonderfully juxtaposes the two wholly opposing approaches to farming, as tempers fray, wild animals run amok, and the land is radically transformed.

The two Dereks’ story will at turns amuse, entertain and provoke thought about environmental issues and the future of farming.

Award-winning director James Dawson celebrates the potential for understanding in this wonderful film about land use and farming, told by farmers. Packed to the brim with English humour, Derek vs Derek is essential viewing.

id: Leadership and Management Part 3-AREA Meetings and Events, 1 O'Reily Ave, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Leadership and Management Part 3
venue: AREA Meetings and Events, 1 O'Reily Ave, Wellington
long_description:
Leaders today are expected to be the driving force of their teams. They are constantly under pressure to lead effectively in a business environment that is characterised by constant change. Our leadership and management courses offer participants the opportunity to develop the necessary skills to embrace this challenge and lead their teams through these times with confidence and pride.

Our Leadership & Management - Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people already in a leadership/management position, or those about to take up a new role, who want to explore the latest thinking and models for effective management and leadership and build on the techniques acquired in our Part 1 and 2 workshops.

In today’s world, emotional Intelligence is a critical and powerful component of effective leadership. This 2-day course will equip leaders with the skills to become more ‘people smart’ by developing ways to lead with emotional intelligence. Participants will also learn how to inspire their people with a shared vision and align teams to company goals, along with the tools to lead and manage change, ways to become a more influential and persuasive leader and the tools to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace.

long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Edinburgh International Film Festival -

This enchanting adaptation of Jay Parini’s semi-fictional memoir is filled with warmth, wit, and beautiful scenery from the Scottish countryside.

As a young doctoral student in the 1970s, Parini (Fionn Whitehead, Dunkirk) was somehow partnered on a road trip through the Scottish Highlands with the literary icon Jorge Luis Borges (Luis Gnecco).

Parini is both bewildered and enchanted by his eccentric companion, the blind poet’s presence leading to amusing and even poignant adventures. Over the course of an eventful journey, the two forge a deep connection, woven with poetry, music, and a touch of melancholy.

Borges and Me revels in the splendour of its locations. Gorgeously photographed, the raw beauty of the rural Scottish landscape translates beautifully to the big screen.

Whitehead and Gnecco are superb as the central pair, with a terrific supporting cast including Alan Cumming, Peter Mullan and Freya Mavor. Pack your bags, this is a road trip you can’t afford to miss.

long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Telluride Film Festival -
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Toronto International Film Festival -

Andrew Scott is astonishing in this powerful, deeply moving, and inspiring story of the actor Ian Charleson, who faced incredible odds while preparing to play Hamlet at the National Theatre.

Scott plays Ian Charleson in 1989, discontented with his career stagnation despite early success in the Best Picture winners Chariots of Fire (1981) and Ghandi (1982).

The chance of a lifetime soon comes along, when Daniel Day-Lewis unexpectedly departs the role of Hamlet at London’s National Theatre. But dream collides with nightmare, as Charleson faces a devastating AIDS diagnosis. Determined to seize his last opportunity for meaning, Charleson delivers a courageous performance that becomes a source of healing and inspiration for those around him.

Alongside a career-best turn from Scott, Olivia Colman delivers a masterclass performance as a doctor treating Charleson and fellow gay men during the HIV epidemic.

Elsinore is generating Oscar buzz after it received a massive standing ovation at its recent Toronto International Film Festival screening. Don’t miss this stirring and transcendent film.

id: Colourful Enamel Jewellery Day-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Colourful Enamel Jewellery Day
venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
long_description:
Learn to create beautiful enamelled jewellery with Lisa Sinclair.

Join us for a full-day enamelling workshop where you’ll explore colour, texture, and fire to create vibrant enamelled jewellery in copper or silver.

This hands-on class focuses on the fundamentals of enamelling, showing you how to apply, fire, and layer enamel to achieve rich, expressive surfaces. You’ll make a simple yet beautifully textured pendant or pair of earrings, then learn how to add a pop (or flood!) of colour to bring your piece to life.

Beginners to metalwork are very welcome - pre-formed shapes are available so you can focus on experimenting with colour, pattern, and mark-making. If you have some metalworking experience, you’re encouraged to take things further by creating and texturing your own metal forms before enamelling.

This is a playful, creative workshop and an ideal class for anyone who loves working with colour, surface, and experimentation - whether you’re new to enamels or keen to deepen your skills.

What you’ll learn:
The basics of enamelling on copper and silver
How to prepare metal for enamelling
Applying enamel using different techniques
Firing enamel and building up layers of colour
Creating texture and pattern in metal
Tips for achieving clean, vibrant enamel finishes

The class fee covers enamel materials but NOT metals. Students can choose from a range of pre-cut copper blanks or use their own copper sheet. Findings and chains are available to purchase at a range of good prices to suit all budgets.

Kids aged approximately 12+ are welcome. Any participant under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

For health and safety reasons, students must wear sturdy closed-toe shoes.

name: Posture Perfection Is Possible
venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
long_description:
Are you a computer slouch, feeling stiff and tense at work? Do you find it difficult to maintain a good posture? Does your posture cause back, neck or shoulder tension? Would you like to enjoy more freedom in everyday activities?

Under the guidance of an experienced teacher, we'll explore movement in ways that help you reduce tense unhelpful habits. Movement lessons are done on the floor or sitting on a chair and are based on the pioneering work of Israeli physicist and engineer Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais. This workshop is suitable for all ages (over 16) and fitness levels.

Outcomes
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:

Identify and reduce muscle tension
Move with more lightness and freedom
Improve your posture
Describe some basic anatomy
Have tools to use at home and at work

Bring two blankets (or a mat and a blanket) and wear loose, warm and comfortable clothing. Tea and coffee provided but bring your lunch.

Please note that instructions are given verbally rather than by demonstration, so good hearing and understanding of English is required.

1 Day
Presented by Sue Field.

Judy’s practical and engaging workshop is especially geared toward choral singers. Drawing on current understanding of the ageing voice, it explores the physiological changes that occur in both the brain and vocal mechanism over time, and offers practical strategies to help maintain vocal health, flexibility, and confidence. Participants will have the opportunity to apply these ideas through a series of guided group singing activities and vocal exercises.

Judy Bellingham is a respected singer, teacher, adjudicator, examiner, and presenter. Although retired from full-time academic and performance roles, she remains deeply committed to the transformative power of the human voice, Judy maintains a thriving private teaching studio and is a sought-after presenter of workshops and masterclasses throughout New Zealand and internationally.

One name. Two champions. BAFTA-nominated filmmaker Alex Holmes delivers the definitive portrait of how Damon Hill overcame the loss of his legendary father, Graham Hill, and followed in his footsteps to become a Formula 1 world champion himself.

Featuring exclusive interviews with Damon and his family, Hill is a gripping documentary that charts the racing legend’s journey through tragedy, pressure, and some of the most iconic moments in F1 history.

Discover the inside story of how Damon fought a furious battle with Michael Schumacher, and dealt with the death of his teammate Ayrton Senna, who tragically lost his life at 34.

Hill places an insightful focus on who Damon is as a person - his hopes, joys, insecurities, and heartbreak. This engaging approach creates an emotional narrative that captures the attention of both F1 devotees and the uninitiated alike.

With a seamless blend of high-octane Formula 1 footage and intimate home-movie moments, Hill is pacy, polished, and unmissable.

long_description:
The Invisible Man (1933) | Halloween Film Night at Aratoi

THE INVISIBLE MAN
1933 | 71 mins
Starring Claude Rains
Saturday 31 October | Doors open 7:15pm | Film starts 7.30pm
Aratoi Wairarapa Museum of Art and History
$5 Admission

This Halloween, The Story Studio invites you to step into the shadows for one of Universal’s great horror classics.

James Whale’s The Invisible Man (1933) stars Claude Rains as Jack Griffin, a scientist who discovers a way to make himself invisible. What begins as a scientific breakthrough soon becomes a terrifying descent into obsession, power and madness.

Based on H.G. Wells’ 1897 novel, The Invisible Man remains one of the defining films of Universal’s classic horror era. Claude Rains never appears visibly on screen as the Invisible Man, yet his voice and performance create one of cinema’s most memorable monsters.

Join us at Aratoi for a special Halloween screening in the gallery foyer.

Bring your friends, settle in and revisit a genuine piece of horror history on the big screen.

Presented by The Story Studio as part of a weekend of Halloween film events across the Wairarapa.

id: After God-Circa Theatre, 1 Taranaki St, Wellington-Event Finder
name: After God
venue: Circa Theatre, 1 Taranaki St, Wellington
long_description:
From the creators of the wildly praised, fiercely original verbatim plays TRANSMISSION and TRANSMISSION:BETA, the New Zealand premiere of AFTER GOD is a theatrical journey across continents and conversations, with one of Aotearoa’s most distinguished actors, Michael Hurst, joining director Miranda Harcourt and writer Stuart McKenzie to explore big questions about meaning, madness and metaphysics.

With a hungry mind and burning questions, McKenzie hits the road — travelling from Wellington to Kathmandu, London and New York. Along the way, he encounters a vivid cast of real-life characters: theologians, Tibetan rinpoches, philosophers, cosmologists, taxi drivers, hotel receptionists, a famous singing nun — and his own mother. Each has their own radically different way of making sense of existence.

Created entirely from real conversations, AFTER GOD is a new verbatim theatre work, transforming interviews, ideas and personal stories into an exhilarating theatrical experience.

It’s a funny, provocative and hopeful exploration of what we believe, what keeps us going and what it means to be alive right now.

long_description:
About the Half-Day Course

Is it possible to find genuine peace in this digital age?

We live in a fast-paced world filled with distractions, constant notifications, and endless comparisons. It’s easy to feel overwhelmed, restless, and disconnected from ourselves. But peace doesn’t come from switching off the world—it comes from changing the way we relate to it. Buddha’s timeless wisdom shows us how to stay calm and centred, no matter what is happening around us.

At this half-day course, Buddhist monk and National Spiritual Director, Gen Kelsang Rabten will share practical Buddhist insights and guide simple meditations to help us step back from the busyness of life, quiet the inner noise, and reconnect with clarity, focus, and joy.

Everyone welcome.

id: Anthonie Tonnon presents Cinematographer-Hannah Playhouse, 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Anthonie Tonnon presents Cinematographer
venue: Hannah Playhouse, 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington
long_description:
Taite Music Prize-winning songwriter Anthonie Tonnon presents his immersive new live show, Cinematographer.

Three years in the making, Cinematographer combines live electronic music, cinematic storytelling and visual design into an immersive performance. Featuring visual DJing by Erica Sklenars, videography by Theo Taylor, styling by Karlya Smith and design by Daniel Alexander, the show sees Tonnon playing the roles of DJ, singer, documentarian and revolutionary lecturer.

The show explores two timelines: the Situationist International in France and Italy during the 1960s, and Whanganui, New Zealand at the turn of the millennium - a mysterious, forgotten city where a new battle is being waged against what Guy Debord famously called The Society of the Spectacle.

Swapping his guitar for a vocoder, and transforming two Synthstrom Deluges into honorary turntables, Tonnon connects these seemingly distant worlds through the musical language of turn-of-the-millennium dance culture.

"Cinematographer is part film, part francophile performance lecture, part disco club set," says Tonnon. "It's a world that we've built for this new music, exploring some newfound passions – the French avant-garde, cinema, urban politics of the 1960s, turn-of-the-millennium dance culture and documentary films, and the glorious, mystifying city of Whanganui."

The ambitious audiovisual performance introduces an entirely new body of work developed with Tonnon's band and longtime producer Jonathan Pearce. The new single and video "Executive Assistant" offers the first glimpse into this new world - Tonnon's first new music in three years.

Doors open: 8:45 I Show 9:15PM

Unallocated seating and standing available.

Early Bird tickets available until Monday 10 August or until allocation sells out.

id: Hapua Farm walk with Wairarapa Catchment Collective-Hāpua farm, 1094 Masterton Castlepoint Rd, Tauweru, Masterton-Event Finder
name: Hapua Farm walk with Wairarapa Catchment Collective
venue: Hāpua farm, 1094 Masterton Castlepoint Rd, Tauweru, Masterton
long_description:
Discover the beauty of Hāpua Farm, a property that combines rolling farmland with wetlands, native bush, and sweeping views of the surrounding hill country.
Led by Michael Birch, the walk begins on the farm’s airstrip, offering beautiful views of the Tararua Ranges before descending through farm tracks, open paddocks, and bush trails.

Along the way, explore wetlands created by large landslides 11,000–12,000 years ago, and continue east to two protected QEII covenant areas of native bush.
Here, you’ll encounter towering totara, matai, and kahikatea, as well as abundant birdlife including kererū and tūī.
Last year's participants had rave reviews of this walk!

Note: the terrain is a mixture of moderate and steep hills, including rough ground and bush tracks. You will need to climb over fences using stiles.

Elemental cooking. Generous feasting. A little fire-fuelled theatre.

Follow the smoke to Alexia.

Bookings essential.

long_description:
Join us to celebrate a very big building's very big birthday!

Old Government Buildings turns 150 this year. Opened in 1876, Pōneke's most eye-catching Neo-Renaissance icon is one of the world's largest wooden buildings. Once home to the entire Wellington-based civil service, today the building houses Te Herenga Waka Victoria University's Faculty of Law, and is very proudly cared for by Heritage New Zealand.

We're celebrating this big anniversary with a day of tours, talks, family activities, competitions, and, of course, birthday cake!

Visit our website for a developing schedule of events, and to book heritage tours and special attic tours.

This event is proudly presented by Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga as part of Wellington Heritage Festival 2026.

name: 30 Years With The Pūkorokoro Shorebird Centre - Forest & Bird Event
venue: The Garden Room at St Peter’s on Willis, 90 Ghuznee St, Te Aro, Wellington
long_description:
Keith Woodley has served as the Manager of the Pūkorokoro Shorebird Centre since 1993. Over more than three decades dedicated to coastal ecology and bird conservation, he has become a leading voice for shorebird protection in New Zealand.

The Wellington Branch of Forest and Bird invite you to join us as Keith shares insights into the world of New Zealand’s migratory shorebirds. Drawing on decades of observation and research, Keith will highlight the extraordinary migrations of species like the bar-tailed godwit and the unique adaptations of the endemic wrybill - the only bird in the world with a side-curved bill. He will discuss the seasonal rhythms of the Firth of Thames, and the work of Pūkorokoro Miranda Naturalists’ Trust in the East Asian Australasian Flyway, and how local community conservation efforts protect these critical coastal habitats.

id: Tuesday Jewellery-making: 8-week course for Beginners-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Tuesday Jewellery-making: 8-week course for Beginners
venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
long_description:
This class is beginner level only, with each student following the class project.

It starts Tue 27 October and runs for 8 weeks ill Tue 15 December, 5.30pm - 8pm.

Our popular weeknight classes are the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

The stone-setting process teaches you many fundamental techniques in one project!

We start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering.

Then we move on to making a practice ring set with a Cabochon stone (a cabochon has a flat bottom and a smooth, domed top) in a Bezel Setting.

As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love. This way, you will learn the basics as you go on your practice ring, before taking the next step in costly silver.

This class has all materials included in the class fee!

Each student receives a carefully curated materials pack including copper or brass, sterling and fine silver for your ring-making projects, as well as two stones from our supply so you get a good stone for your level of experience.

We have loads of gorgeous stones of a range of colours, and they are all appropriate for beginner settings.

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, Afterpay or PayPal on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time, please email us to arrange this ;)

name: Stacking Rings - Taster
venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
long_description:
Create your own ring stack from copper, brass, and sterling silver in this fun and rewarding jewellery workshop.

Guided by experienced and supportive tutors, you’ll be introduced to the fundamental skills of jewellery making while creating a small collection of rings to take home.

During this 3-hour class, you’ll learn how to measure your finger, cut metal to size, and add textures and patterns using hammers and punches. You’ll also be shown how to solder your rings with a jeweller’s torch, before finishing them with filing, sanding, and polishing techniques.

By the end of the session, you’ll have crafted a thick sterling silver ring and a stack of copper or brass rings, including two plain round wires to texture as you like, and a choice of decorative brass pearl wire or square wire.

This class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends, or visitors wanting a memorable creative experience. Many students find jewellery making a mindful activity, offering a chance to slow down, work with their hands, and enjoy the rhythm of making.

The class fee includes all materials and consumables, such as solder, sandpaper, and polishing materials. Extra silver and other metals will be available for purchase in the studio for those who would like to expand their collection or upgrade one of their brass or copper wires to a second silver one.

Children aged 12 and over are welcome. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

long_description:
An afternoon of exploratory improvisations and new compositions at Karori's Futuna Chapel. Doors open at 2pm, music starts 2:30pm.

Doxing Ur Mum is a new song cycle composed by Mallory Elmo, with lyrics by poet and textile artist Anne Amber, performed by Kassandra Wang (mezzo-soprano) and Antonia Grant (violin).

The fruit of three years of collaboration, these songs speak aphoristically of everyday, intimate, and queer personal experiences in the city of Pōneke. Kassandra and Antonia will also perform a new work by Ōtautahi-based composer Luka Reardon and a collaborative composition of their own.

Multifaceted musicians lucky pollock, Amy-Jane, and Tristan Carter will join forces on flute, violin, keyboard, and more, exploring ambient free improvisation through their shared classical, popular, and experimental backgrounds.

scramble204, Shay Patel (guitar)'s project with Vinnie Whitehead (guitar) and Alex Hoare (cello), will present an iteration of their Dialogues series.

id: Textured Bracelets-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Textured Bracelets
venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
long_description:
This lively, hands-on workshop is designed for complete beginners, but it’s also a great opportunity for more experienced students to enjoy a creative session making their own unique bangle!

Everyone will leave with a beautifully finished bracelet of their own preferred texture.

We’ll begin by experimenting on a sample strip of copper, where you’ll practice creating textures using hammers, punches and stamps. Once you’re confident, you’ll move on to your main project: a 3mm wide flat strip bracelet in either sterling silver or copper, crafted entirely by you from start to finish. Along the way, you’ll learn essential jewellery-making skills including measuring, texturing, soldering, shaping, and finishing.

Students are free to personalise their bangle with textures or stamped designs. This could be a simple hammered finish, decorative patterns, or meaningful words, names, dates, or poetry lines - making your bracelet truly one of a kind.
Beginners will work with the 3mm strip provided, ensuring a rewarding project that’s manageable to complete. Wider metal is much harder to form and solder, so we are learning to walk before we can run ;)

Copper is included in the course fee; if you wish to work in silver, you can purchase it on the day.

Experienced students may choose to challenge themselves by making a wider bracelet from a flat strip or by creating additional bangles in silver wire. (Please note: extra silver for wider bangles is available to purchase at the workshop for experienced students only, and let us know if you wish to go wider so we can make sure we have the strip in stock.)

This workshop is a taster class: perfect for anyone seeking a fun, creative experience with a beautiful result, or for those looking to dip their toes into jewellery making and build foundational skills.

name: Chaosium Table Top RPG Conference
venue: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, 55 Cable St, Wellington
long_description:
A weekend filled with cosmic horror, knightly deeds, questing for Runes and much more!

Chaosium Con NZ is a unique international convention dedicated to the fans of Chaosium’s legendary games, including Call of Cthulhu, RuneQuest, Pendragon, Time Without Tide, Age of Vikings and many others.

The iconic Museum of New Zealand, Te Papa Tongarewa, will become a gathering place for investigators, storytellers, and dreamers from across the globe. Surrounded by the stories and the cultural heritage of Aotearoa New Zealand, attendees will experience Chaosium in an inspiring setting where imagination, history, and community come together.

What can I do at Chaosium Con? Your badge covers entry to the convention where you can sign up to play a plethora of games, listen to talks from the leading industry TTRPG professionals and win prizes! Each day of the convention has three session time slots, each running for 3-4 hours, so you can play a variety of games with different people.

Meet the minds behind the Mythos!
Neil Robinson - CEO of Chaosium, Producer of Age of Vikings & Basic Roleplaying, Writer.
Michael O'Brien - Vice President of Chaosium. Line Editor - Runequest, Producer of Call of Cthulhu
Susan O'Brien - Fiction Editor. Editor Credo: The Board Game.
Jason Durall - Line Editor for Basic Roleplaying
Paula Deming - The Glass Cannon Network, Good Time Society, Graveyards of Arkham
Sean Branney - Film-maker, co-founder of H.P. Lovecraft Historical Society

And even more minds of the mythos! Find out more on our website: http://sites.google.com/chaosium.com/chaosium-con-nz?usp=sharing

Looking to GM Games? Want to run a game at Chaosium Con?
Sign up using this form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1a4cgLaDlbGqRlEWeFD-GV_CbKdQspiG0wGs6yJ8hjFU/edit?edit_requested=true%22

id: From Plate to Page: An Evening with Peter Gordon-Samuel Marsden Collegiate School, 35 Marsden Avenue, Karori, Wellington-Event Finder
name: From Plate to Page: An Evening with Peter Gordon
venue: Samuel Marsden Collegiate School, 35 Marsden Avenue, Karori, Wellington
long_description:
Peter Gordon is a chef, restaurateur, writer and fusion pioneer whose eclectic cuisine has had global reach. Join us at this special fundraising event for Katherine Mansfield House & Garden to hear about the books, travel, people and experiences that have shaped his life.

For forty years Peter has gathered ingredients, textures and techniques from around the world and brought them to diners at his award-winning restaurants such as The Sugar Club and The Providores, and into homes through his eight cookbooks. He has cooked for world leaders including Queen Elizabeth II and Barack Obama, presented shows for the Discovery Channel and Whakaata Māori (Māori Television), and appeared on the shows of Nigel Slater and Jamie Oliver in the UK and as a guest judge on MasterChef NZ. He is also the founder of the hugely successful UK charity event Who’s Cooking Dinner? and its NZ equivalent Dining for a Difference.

The evening will begin with a glass of Hunter’s Wines’ award-winning MiruMiru™ and delicious canapés in the foyer (a non-alcoholic option will also be available). We will then move into the auditorium for a conversation with Peter hosted by Katherine Mansfield House & Garden Director Cherie Jacobson.

This event is being held to raise funds for our Category 1 Historic Place and writer’s museum in Thorndon, which is open six days a week. We offer an annual programme of events and activities designed to encourage creativity and we host school and tour groups to share the life, literature and legacy of Katherine Mansfield.

id: Duntulm Farm hilltop circuit tramp-Duntulm Farm, 820 Mangatarere Valley Road, West Taratahi, Carterton-Event Finder
name: Duntulm Farm hilltop circuit tramp
venue: Duntulm Farm, 820 Mangatarere Valley Road, West Taratahi, Carterton
long_description:
Explore the regenerating and mature bush on Duntulm Carbon Farm, with some of the tramp exploring the adjacent Tararua Forest Park. Mostly on single footpaths and some on farm tracks.
We should see mature rata, kahikatea, totara, rimu, miro, native clematis, possibly mistletoe and various orchids.
There will be extensive views both over the Wairarapa Plains and up to Taratahi/Mt Holdsworth.
The walk will cross the new bridge, go through a shallow crossing of Kiddie Creek, up into the "dress circle" near point 637, along to Holdsworth lookout, down to Duntulm Cottage for a cuppa, followed by a flattish walk out on farm tracks or an optional extra tramp up to pt 533 and down a different track back to the bridge.
Although there have been walks on Duntulm Farm most Wairarapa Walking Festivals, this is a different and fairly challenging route. We will take it reasonably slowly!

Terrain notes: steep hills, stream crossings, scrambly paths through the bush.
Have you comepleted a half-day tramp in the last 6 months?
Once registered, you will sent details on what to bring, suggested clothing, food, water and will need to supply an emergency contact person.

name: Bad Apples- British and Irish Film Festival
venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Toronto International Film Festival -

Oscar-nominee Saoirse Ronan delivers one of her most daring and memorable roles in the satirical thriller Bad Apples, a bold and timely film that challenges how deeply we hold our core beliefs.

Ronan plays Maria, a primary school teacher whose classroom is thrown into chaos by Danny, an exceptionally disruptive and foul-mouthed student.

Maria reaches her breaking point after Danny has a violent run-in with another student, and taking a drastic course of action, traps him in her home.

In Danny’s absence, the classroom begins to thrive; the children flourish academically, and both parents and school staff celebrate the incredible turnaround. But with everyone else convinced the school’s biggest problem has finally been solved, Maria now finds herself trapped in an increasingly preposterous moral dilemma.

Swedish-born director Jonatan Etzler injects scathing Scandi humour into this daring psychological comedy, which is sure to become one of the year’s most talked-about films.

id: Rathkeale Christmas Fête 2026-Rathkeale College Auditorium, Willow Park Drive, Masterton-Event Finder
name: Rathkeale Christmas Fête 2026
venue: Rathkeale College Auditorium, Willow Park Drive, Masterton
long_description:
Welcome to the Rathkeale Christmas Fête 2026.

Walk through the gates of Rathkeale College on 7 November and be welcomed by a diverse range of colourful stalls, the aroma of freshly cooked food, and plenty of festive inspiration.

Now in its 23rd year, the Christmas Fête has become a must-do event on the Wairarapa spring calendar. Stallholders travel from around the North Island to sell their wares and offer Christmas shoppers plenty of inspiration. From festive decorations, clothing, arts and crafts, to flowers, toys, and plants, there is something for everyone.

Gourmet food is always a highlight at the Fête. Think freshly made gourmet burgers, lamb and mint sausages, salads, and the ever-popular berries and ice cream. There is always a huge variety of flavours to tempt the taste buds. Devonshire teas and home baking served in the Rathkeale Homestead rose garden is a time-honoured tradition, while refreshing cold drinks can be enjoyed as visitors listen to live music performed by students at various times throughout the day. The popular Christmas cake stall features again this year, but visitors are encouraged to get in early, as the cakes often sell out by midday.

The beauty of this Fête is that it’s a day out for the whole family. In addition to the 120-plus stalls, there is plenty to entertain children, including a barrel train ride, face painting, and magic shows throughout the day.

Visitors can also explore the beautiful, expansive grounds of Rathkeale College, including the school gardens designed by Alfred Buxton, the recently installed Paul Dibble sculpture The Choice, the Greek Amphitheatre, and the 3km eco-trail, which weaves through large stands of native trees, including ancient kahikatea.

EFTPOS is available, but visitors are encouraged to bring cash.

Koha / gold coin entry

Rathkeale College is a five-minute drive north of Masterton in the Wairarapa.

venue: Ivy Bar and Cabaret, 63 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington
long_description:
Back by popular demand, join us this November for Coven Saloon, a Coyote Ugly themed night. Don't fight the moonlight and be there! Cowboy boots are optional but the best dressed will be rewarded.

Wet t-shirt comp, body shots and surprises in store. Follow us on Instagram for more event info.

Coven is a party for Sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people. Tickets are pay as you wish or koha on the door.

More info about Coven:

Coven Kaupapa
For queer women and gender minorities, spaces like this are rare, vital, and sometimes, life-changing. In a world that constantly centers cishet norms, Coven offers a space where we are the default – where you can fully show up as yourself, be seen, celebrated and surrounded by YOUR community.

Coming Solo? You’re Not Alone.
Don’t be nervous if you’re planning to come on your own – Coven is built for connection. Whether it’s your first queer event or your hundredth, you’ll be surrounded by a community that gets it. From the moment you arrive, there’ll be friendly faces, welcoming vibes, and plenty of chances to mingle, and connect. Coven is about belonging – and there’s a place here for you.

For many in our Coven, this is one of the only opportunities we feel comfortable enough to experience nightlife free from the male gaze, tokenism, fear, or the need to shrink ourselves to fit in. It’s a space where sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people aren’t just welcomed – we are centered. It’s for those who are often pushed to the margins, who rarely feel represented in “inclusive” spaces that still cater to the mainstream.

This night exists because we need it – and because we create it, together.

Accessibility
This event is located down a flight of stairs. Have specific accessibility needs? Reach out at coveneventswellington@gmail.com

Everyone is welcome to this fun class! Whether you have a little more experience, or are starting from scratch, if you want to draw people, this workshop is for you.

In this class, artists will learn and extend their skills with drawing and painting.

Perfect for both beginners and more experienced artists, Ellie will help the students experiment and learn while having fun and creating wonderful pieces of art. Our classes builds self-confidence, traditional techniques, and creative experimentation.

They previously ran Tacit Art Gallery in Hamilton, and have worked at both the Waikato Museum and the Adam Art Gallery.

This event is a fun, safe space for all, including LGBTQ+ and the site includes a gender-neutral bathroom for students.

id: Powell Hut Overnight Tramp-Tararua Forest Park, Mt. Holdsworth Rd, Carterton-Event Finder
name: Powell Hut Overnight Tramp
venue: Tararua Forest Park, Mt. Holdsworth Rd, Carterton
long_description:
Join the Wairarapa Walking Festival on this classic and epic tramp to Powell Hut.

The first day: we will walk from Mt Holdsworth car park up to Powell Hut. This is 5 to 6 hours of uphill tramping, with good tracks and steps. The hut is at the edge of the bush-line with glorious views (and cell phone access).

Powell Hut has (gas) stoves, a wood-burner and bunks with mattresses. There are long-drop toilets and a water tank collecting water from the roof.

The Wairarapa Walking Festival team have booked 20 bunks for this great adventure.

Bring water for the tramp, snacks (muesli bars, dried fruit, nuts, chocolate etc), picnic lunch for both days, dinner and breakfast, plus hot chocolate, tea or coffee. Also, basic toiletries, hut shoes, nightwear, sleeping bags and recommend earplugs.

The second day: depending on the group and the weather we will either return the same way of go onto the alpine tops, look at the alpine flowers and comeback down East Holdsworth track. We should be back at the car park by 3 or 4pm.

Essential to have tramping boots or solid walking shoes, wind and rainproof jackets and merino or fleece layers. A change of clothes to wear in the hut in case you get wet on the walk. Walking poles recommended if you have them.

D.O.C labels this walk an 'intermediate tramping track'. The car park is at 320m elevation and Powell Hut is at 1200m elevation.

Please note - once registered, you will be asked to provide Emergency Contact details of a friend / relative and whether you have been tramping in the last 6 months. The Walk coordinator for WWF will carry a PLB. There is good cell phone coverage from the Hut.

Ticket costs are only to cover bunk costs at hut. Tickets will go off-sale 2 days prior to enable logistics, check the weather for the trip.

Youth between ages of 12 - 16 require an accompanying adult to attend also.

Celia recommends downloading the free iNaturalist app before you go.

id: Finding Matariki: Their nature, and legends.-Stonehenge Aotearoa, 51 Ahiaruhe Rd, Carterton-Event Finder
name: Finding Matariki: Their nature, and legends.
venue: Stonehenge Aotearoa, 51 Ahiaruhe Rd, Carterton
long_description:
Delve into the rich tapestry of Māori and Polynesian astronomy with our engaging evening tour at Stonehenge Aotearoa. While the sacred time for observing Matariki (the Pleiades) traditionally occurs with its early morning rising, these same stars grace the evening sky in November. This presents a unique opportunity for those seeking to explore the cosmos in a comfortable, warm setting as the night sky darkens.

Our tour begins as the sky transitions from twilight to night, creating an ideal environment for stargazing. Guided by knowledgeable astronomers, you will embark on a journey through ancient legends and the physical nature of the stars. This is a time of learning and understanding, where the mysteries of the heavens unfold through captivating stories and scientific insights.

Using laser pointers, our guides will illuminate the constellations, revealing the celestial patterns recognized by Māori and Polynesian navigators for centuries. You’ll learn how these constellations were used not only for navigation but also for marking seasonal changes and significant events. The stories behind these constellations are rich with cultural significance, offering a deeper appreciation for the ingenuity and wisdom of our ancestors.

As you gaze up at the night sky, you’ll discover the intricate connections between the stars and the stories woven into the fabric of Māori and Polynesian heritage. From the celebrated Matariki cluster to other important constellations, each star tells a part of the larger narrative that has guided and inspired generations.

This tour provides a perfect blend of mythology and astronomy, making it suitable for all ages and interests. Whether you are a seasoned stargazer or a curious newcomer, you will find something to fascinate and inspire you. The use of laser pointers enhances the experience, making the constellations easily identifiable and the stories even more vivid.

Join us for an unforgettable evening under the stars at Stonehenge Aotearoa. This is more than just a tour; it’s an immersive experience that connects you to the ancient traditions and the celestial wonders that have shaped our world. Book your spot now and embark on a journey of discovery and enlightenment, where the past meets the present in the most spectacular way.

Please note: All guided tours must be booked in advance.
Tours do not run without prior bookings, and walk-ins cannot be accommodated. These are shared tours, meaning multiple groups may join the same session.

id: This Is Grief: On the Road-Unity Books, 57 Willis St, Wellington-Event Finder
name: This Is Grief: On the Road
venue: Unity Books, 57 Willis St, Wellington
long_description:
Grief is part of being human, but we still struggle to talk about it.
This Is Grief: On the Road is a free community event bringing honest conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them into communities across Aotearoa.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O'Connor for a relaxed, human conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the clichés, timelines and expectations we so often place around it. Kirsten will share from her own experience of grief and from her work writing and talking about loss, before opening the space for conversation and connection.

You don't need to have the right words. You don't need to share anything you don't want to. This is a space for anyone living with loss, or anyone who wants to better understand and support someone who is.

Come along, listen, talk if you'd like to, and be part of a conversation we don't have nearly often enough.

This is a free community event. Registration is recommended as places may be limited.

id: Book Group: The Turn of the Screw by Henry James-The Library, 1/53 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Book Group: The Turn of the Screw by Henry James
venue: The Library, 1/53 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington
long_description:
With our November book group taking place just a few days after Halloween, we'll be discussing the classic ghost story The Turn of the Screw by Henry James. Published in 1898, it quickly became James' most popular work of short fiction.

The gothic horror novella tells of a young governess who arrives at a remote country estate to care for two children, only to become convinced that supernatural forces haunt the grounds. Even its author found it terrifying: “I had to correct the proofs of my ghost story last night,” he told poet Edmund Gosse, “and when I had finished them I was so frightened that I was afraid to go upstairs to bed!”

The group previously read Henry James' The Portrait of a Lady way back at the beginning of 2014.

Project Gutenberg link for those e-reading:
https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/209

Plus, because it's in the public domain, there are a number of audiobooks on YouTube - perhaps the perfect way to experience a ghost story...

Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read works that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

RSVP
Bookings essential. Get your free ticket by clicking 'Register' above. Limited places.

If you've signed up, but things change and you're not going to be able to make it along, please email classiclitwgtn@gmail.com as we may be able to make more spaces available for others.

VENUE
We meet in the ‘Games Room’, The Library bar's private area overlooking Courtenay Place. After you enter the bar, head to your right (up the step) and through a smaller space with booths to the large carpeted space beyond (behind the big wooden sliding door).

ABOUT US
Wellington Classic Literature Club has been running for more than a decade - since the start of 2013 - and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers who join us for particular books or simply when it suits.

Andrew James from Nottingham, England has been a singer/performer since 1994, Starting his Tribute to Phil Collins and Genesis at the end of 2006.

Andrew has performed for many leading Hotel & Holiday chains in the UK, including Park Resorts, Haven, Butlins, Pontins and numerous smaller venues, private & Public. id: A Peek into Pencarrow Lighthouse - Wellington Heritage Festival-Pencarrow Lighthouse, Muritai Rd, Pencarrow Head, Lower Hutt-Event Finder
name: A Peek into Pencarrow Lighthouse - Wellington Heritage Festival
venue: Pencarrow Lighthouse, Muritai Rd, Pencarrow Head, Lower Hutt
long_description:
Located on beautiful and often windswept Pencarrow Head, New Zealand's oldest lighthouse dates to 1859.

Walk or cycle to Aotearoa's first lighthouse, then chat with knowledgeable guides about the history, construction and stories behind this unique Pōneke landmark, and explore the interior, usually restricted for public access.

Pencarrow Lighthouse open day is free to attend, however a koha is always appreciated.

Please note the track up to Pencarrow Lighthouse is steep and can be muddy. Ensure adequate footwear is worn. The weather can be changeable, and we recommend bring along snacks, water and a wind jacket. There are no toilets along the track up to Pencarrow Lighthouse or at the lighthouse itself. Public toilets are located near the end of Pencarrow Coast Road.

This event is proudly presented by Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga as part of Wellington Heritage Festival 2026.

venue: Michael Fowler Centre, 111 Wakefield Street, Wellington
long_description:
Ross Harris Concerto for Orchestra (World Premiere)
Saint-Saëns Piano Concerto No. 5 Egyptian
Elgar Enigma Variations

Edward Elgar’s greatest masterpiece remains swathed in mystery.

His Enigma Variations, a set of 14 variations on a theme you never actually hear, has been the subject of both intense scrutiny and great love, thanks to the compositional genius and throbbing heart pulsing in these compelling variations.

Similarly, Saint-Saëns’ Fifth Piano Concerto has beguiled audiences with its Eastern-inspired sounds — hence its Egyptian nickname. To weave his own spell on us, legendary pianist Sir Stephen Hough returns to our shores. Praised by Limelight for possessing “an other-worldly stillness and strength [and] the perfect technique combined with the utmost poetic fluency”, Hough promises to transport us to another world.

We proudly premiere Ross Harris’ Concerto for Orchestra. A four-time winner of the SOUNZ Contemporary Award, Harris’ artistry and bold vision electrifies this newly commissioned work, driving the orchestra to new heights.

name: Heritage Trees in the Wellington Botanic Garden
venue: Wellington Botanic Garden, 101 Glenmore St, Kelburn, Wellington
long_description:
Join us for an enlightening heritage walk through the historic Wellington Botanic Garden, sharing the stories of heritage trees.

In 1868, James Hector was appointed manager of the then 13-acre (5.66 hectares) area set aside for the Wellington Botanic Garden. It is now home to some of the oldest exotic trees in New Zealand, and is both a Garden of National Significance and the first public garden in New Zealand to be classified as an historic area by the New Zealand Historic Places Trust.

The one-hour heritage walk will focus on many of the notable specimen trees planted since 1868.

Meet at the Founders' Entrance, Glenmore Street.
Cost: $10 or Free for Friends – bookings required (you’ll get the option to choose your ticket type after clicking ‘Buy Tickets’)

This is part of the regular walks run by the Friends of the Wellington Botanic Garden. They run throughout the year with a different topic every time.

Join the Friends for only $30 a year and all the walks will be free, as well as other great benefits.

name: Louis Baker – 'Trouble' Album Release Tour
venue: Meow Nui, 92 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, Wellington
long_description:
Critically acclaimed multi-instrumentalist, songwriter and producer Louis Baker returns with a nationwide headline tour celebrating his forthcoming second studio album, Trouble, released on 9 October. To celebrate the release of Trouble, Baker will embark on a 9-date nationwide tour across Aotearoa throughout October and November, performing songs from the new album alongside favourites from across his catalogue. The tour begins with a series of intimate solo performances before expanding into full-band shows.

Written, produced and arranged by Baker across 2024 and 2025 from his studio in Titahi Bay, Wellington, Trouble is rooted in timeless songwriting, blending retro-soul influences with contemporary production. Across nine songs, the album unfolds as Baker's most assured work to date, balancing social observation with reflections on love, resilience and the work of confronting himself.

Over the past decade, Baker has established himself as one of Aotearoa New Zealand's most distinctive contemporary soul artists. Renowned for his captivating live performances, expressive guitar playing and rich, soulful vocals, he has built a loyal international following through sheer authenticity and craft. He has toured extensively throughout Australia, Europe, the UK and Aotearoa, sharing stages with artists including Jordan Rakei, Allen Stone and Jamie Lidell, and most recently joined Fat Freddy's Drop on their international tours across Europe, Australia and the UK.

17 October – Rhyme X Reason, Wānaka *solo

23 October – Totara St, Mount Maunganui **

id: Carkeek Revealed: A Walk Through Wairarapa’s Astronomical Heritage-Pae Tū Mōkai O Tauira Whare, 23 N Soldiers Settlement Road, Featherston-Event Finder
name: Carkeek Revealed: A Walk Through Wairarapa’s Astronomical Heritage
venue: Pae Tū Mōkai O Tauira Whare, 23 N Soldiers Settlement Road, Featherston
long_description:
Step into the past as we uncover the story of Stephen Carkeek and his passion for the night sky. The Carkeek observatory - the oldest surviving example of an astronomical observatory in New Zealand - was rediscovered in 1987.

Take a family-friendly guided walk to see the remains, now covered and protected, and hear stories from Stephen's descendants as well as passionate local advocates keen to protect this piece of history. Enjoy a morning tea and listen to a reading of the children's book The Lost Star of Featherston.

Built in circa 1867 on a farm south of the Wairarapa town of Featherston, the Carkeek Observatory possesses outstanding historical significance as Aotearoa/New Zealand’s earliest surviving astronomical observatory. Built by civil servant, timeball instigator and amateur astronomer Stephen Carkeek, the place reflects the crucial role of amateur practitioners in the foundation and development of science in this country.

Koha.

venue: Pukaha Mount Bruce National Wildlife Centre, 85379 State Highway 2, Mount Bruce, Masterton
long_description:
As evening settles over the forest, head out along Pūkaha’s Loop Track, normally only accessible during the day, and make your way to the top of the reserve.
Along the way, experience the changing sights and sounds of the ngahere as daylight fades and the forest comes alive at night.

At the top, pause to enjoy a warming kawakawa tea and light snack before beginning the return journey under the night sky.
The experience will also include a short presentation exploring Pūkaha, our connection to the ngahere and the importance of protecting our dark skies.

This is a unique opportunity to experience a different side of Pūkaha and see what happens when the daytime visitors have gone home.

long_description:
You’ve used AI – now make it work on your actual job. In this hands-on full-day workshop, Jon Bell will guide you through building a real AI system around your work: connectors, your own documents and tools, Anthropic skills, and Claude Design. Intake form required before class. (NZ Citizens and residents pay $250 with ID.)

You’ve been using AI for a while – maybe daily. You know how to prompt. But you’re still doing one-shot chats when your work deserves a proper system. This masterclass changes that.

Before you arrive, you’ll fill in a short intake form – what you do, what you want AI for, and what you can’t do (paste client data into public ChatGPT, work outside regulated tools, etc.). Jon reads every submission before class and shapes the day around the room. We won’t be doing a generic feature tour; the day is built to be a hands-on and customised workshop.

We’ll spend the day wiring AI into your actual work: the Claude desktop app, connectors to the tools you already use, a project built around your real documents and tasks, and Claude Design. You’ll leave with a working AI system to improve your life and work.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:

• Set up the Claude desktop app with Chat, Co-work, and Code – ready for real work

• Enable and use connectors (Gmail, Drive, calendar) – and know which ones to leave off

• Build a Claude project around your own documents and tasks, with voice input and plan mode

• Write operating rules for your workspace – constraints, verification triggers, what never goes in public chat

• Discover and run Anthropic-provided skills on your real task

• Stress-test your output with synthetic personas before you ship

• Produce polished visual artifacts with Claude Design

• Apply professional judgement: when to delegate, when to verify, when not to use AI at all

Please bring: A laptop (Co-work and Code need a keyboard). The Claude desktop app installed and signed in. A paid Claude subscription (Pro or Team) – required for connectors, Co-work, and skills. Your intake form submitted at least 3 days before class. One real task you want to work on.

A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Prerequisites
Have completed Getting the Most from AI (Tier 1) – or equivalent: regular Claude or ChatGPT use, basic security habits, and some experience with Projects or custom instructions. This is not a beginner class.

long_description:
We're BAAAAAAAACK!

This year we lost two icons, outspoken supporters, unwavering allies of the LGBTQIA+ communities - Dolly Parton, Country Music Queen, and Tim Curry aka Frankenfurter from The Rocky Horror Picture Show. They died a day apart and devastated countless fans around the world.

Our dance party this year is a tribute and celebration of their aroha, fierce advocacy, allyship, and unapologetic flamboyant expression of joy. Which one are you?... or are you both?

Whether its big hair and rhinestones or fishnets, corsets, and heavy makeup - you choose your style and we'll do the rest!

We promise a night of absolute banger tunes from Vinyl&Proud, special guest DJ Panda, a cash bar, snacks for sale, a friendly and fabulous vibe, and oh yes, a dance-off and prizes for best costumes!

No BYO, R18 - be prepared to be asked for ID.

All proceeds from the dance will go towards our big ten year anniversary next year.

So come on up to the lab, and see what's on the slab...

There will be VERY limited door sales, no holds.

Just a reminder of our kaupapa / values:

Paekakariki Pride is an inclusive festival - we aim to have safe and welcoming spaces for our LGBTQIA+ communities and allies.
We believe trans women are women, trans men are men, and non-binary identities are valid.
We believe only you can define your sexuality and gender.
We acknowledge the untold harm that colonisation has had on tangata whenua, and in particular on takataapui communities.
We are grateful to mana whenua, Ngati Haumia for their ongoing support and awhi and we show respect and aroha for the whenua that we stand on.
When you attend our events, you do so in support of these values.
If you behave in a way that compromises these values we will respectfully ask you leave our events.
It's our way of creating a safe and loving space in our little corner of the world.
Pride is for everyone

id: Heritage Tour at the Haunted Inverlochy House-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Heritage Tour at the Haunted Inverlochy House
venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
long_description:
Celebrate Halloween with a cuppa and a historic tour of the haunted Inverlochy House. Inverlochy House is a Victorian mansion designed by local architect Thomas Turnbull for the Macdonald family in the late 1870s. In the mid 1920s until 1980 it was divided into nine flats and known as the Inverlochy Flats. Since 1987 it has been the home of Inverlochy Art School. Inverlochy House has had a reputation for being haunted since the 1970s and has been the subject of an ongoing paranormal investigation by several NZ and international groups over the years.

Tour runs for approximately one hour. Stay in town to enjoy dinner at the local cafes in Te Aro.

id: A Wartime Evening at the RSA-Featherston Memorial RSA, 57 Fox St, Featherston-Event Finder
name: A Wartime Evening at the RSA
venue: Featherston Memorial RSA, 57 Fox St, Featherston
long_description:
Experience an evening of wartime food, music and memories at the Featherston RSA, celebrating the stories and spirit of the World War II era. Your evening will be themed around a warrant officers’ and senior NCOs’ mess dinner evening, from within a Second World War air raid shelter. As you eat your meal, your narrator will take you through the years of World War II, from the invasion of Poland and the miracle of Dunkirk, to the Pacific and Monte Cassino, all the way through to VE and VJ Day, plus much more in between.

The food will be loosely based on the type of fare people ate during the years of rationing - think potted meat, bangers and mash, and stewed apples.
Your meal will be slightly different though. Instead of potted meat, you’ll have a delicious pate, accompanied with melba toast and a cherry relish. This will be followed by exquisite gourmet sausages from Greytown Butcher, served with delicious creamed potatoes, peas, and onion gravy. Dessert will be a delectable apple pie, served with a sumptuous vanilla custard. The meal will be rounded off with cheese and biscuits.
You are highly encouraged to wear 1940s attire or military uniform, with a prize for best dressed man and best dressed woman.

Tickets available from EventFinda and the Featherston Memorial RSA - fstnrsaevents@gmail.com

name: Glass Bead-Making Taster - Taster Session!
venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
long_description:
Join us for this fabulous introduction to working with colourful molten glass!

This class is a great way for absolute beginners to get a taste of working with glass to produce beautiful beads that can be used in a myriad of ways, including making a unique gift for your loved one (or yourself!).

As one of the earliest forms of human adornment, beads have long functioned as a way to express individuality, and what better way to do that than to learn to make your own unique beads?

Students are shown correct lampworking techniques to produce several decorative beads in just 3 hours! How many beads you make is up to you; some students make up to 10 while others make fewer using trickier techniques.

Kids over 12 (or so) are welcome to take the class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

long_description:

OFFICIAL SELECTION: Telluride Film Festival -

The latest film from British cinema royalty Danny Boyle (Trainspotting, Slumdog Millionaire), Ink charts the rise of Rupert Murdoch’s notorious newspaper The Sun, and the creation of the UK’s tabloid culture.

Guy Pearce (The Brutalist) stars as Murdoch, alongside Jack O’Connell (Sinners) as newspaper editor Larry Lamb, newly assigned to oversee the fledgling daily paper. Tasked with attracting new readers in the competitive British media market, Lamb devises a new tactic - throw anything onto the page that will turn heads, no matter the veracity.

The Sun sees a massive spike in readership, and this new broad scope allows Jules Davies (Claire Foy) to break through the male-dominated hierarchy. But as the paper circulation grows, so too does the number of its critics.

Already generating awards season buzz, the fast-paced and gripping Ink features riveting performances from its star cast, in a thrilling exploration of this controversial newsroom legacy.

id: Café Scientifiqué: Super El Niño-Southern Cross - Garden Bar & Restaurant, 39 Abel Smith St, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Café Scientifiqué: Super El Niño
venue: Southern Cross - Garden Bar & Restaurant, 39 Abel Smith St, Te Aro, Wellington
long_description:
Join two leading climate scientists bringing perspectives from atmospheric science and oceanography as they explore what a Super El Niño is, and what it could mean for Aotearoa New Zealand.

After brief 10–15 minute opening talks, we’ll pause for drinks before moving into an extended Q&A and kōrero. This is a conversation-led session, with lots of time for your questions and discussion.

Doors open at 5.30 pm, talks begin at 5.45 pm. All welcome—free entry, nibbles provided

Speakers

Professor James Renwick

James is a Professor of Physical Geography at Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington, with a background in atmospheric physics, mathematics, and statistics. He has an interest in many aspects of climate, from the distant past to the near future, with a particular interest in New Zealand's climate.

Professor Craig Stevens

Craig is a Principal Scientist in Marine Physics at Earth Sciences NZ and Professor of Physics at the University of Auckland. His research explores how the ocean stores heat and the influence on the climate system. He has a focus on how to measure this heat content in some of the least observed parts of the ocean.

What is Café Scientifique?

Café Scientifique is a place where anyone can come to explore the latest ideas in science and technology in a relaxed, friendly environment. Each event begind with a short introduction from the speakers, followed by a question-and-answer conversation.

Please note: anyone under the age of 18 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.

Café Scientifique is hosted by Pūtaiao ki te Pāpori—School of Science in Society. For further information, please contact scienceinsociety@vuw.ac.nz.

name: Wheeler's Luck
venue: Studio 73, 73 Main Street, Greytown
long_description:
‘Wheeler’s Luck’
by Nigel Collins, Toby Leach and Damon Andrews

Wheeler’s Luck is a rural NZ comedy set in the Wairarapa and will run for nine performances from 18th November at Studio 73, Greytown.
Auckland developer, Richard Lush, plans to build a seven-storey gaming and entertainment facility, swimming pool, hotel, health spa, and 18-hole golf course in a local town near you, all at the invitation of the Mayor (a keen golfer). The aim is to inject millions into the local economy and create 51.5 new jobs.

The trouble is, the land has been left to the people of the town according to the will of Nora Cox, not the council - a fact that Mayor Duncan Sanderson has tried to keep under wraps. But there’s no chance of secret machinations in this small town, with eccentric local postie Murray Dickie on the case.

To add to his woes, the Mayor is also having trouble with freak weather and regurgitating sewerage, an experience that will resonate with some Wairarapa residents. There’s a brawl in a local pub that conforms only loosely to legal opening hours, and an annual horse race held on the beach.
So the plot unfolds in this Greytown Little Theatre comedy production Wheeler’s Luck, set in Bell End (a small coastal community to be found in Wairarapa) and coming to Greytown’s Studio 73 in November this year.

The play was written by Nigel Collins, Toby Leach and Damon Andrews, each of whom have significant careers in film, television and theatre as actors and playwrights. Nigel and Toby first performed Wheeler’s Luck in 2004, playing all 52 of the characters of the hilarious and complex plot moving between 1882 and the present day.

Five characters will play all the parts, sometimes conversing with themselves, including the roles of animals and faxes and bells, and swiftly moving between genders. The actors are Egan Tearle, Josh Cameron, and three Kuranui College teachers of music, drama, and dance - Lisa McLeod, Juanita McLellan and Alena-Rose Burt.

name: Everybody to Kenmure Street - British and Irish Film Festival
venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
long_description:
OFFICIALSELECTION: Sundance Film Festival -
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Glasgow Film Festival -

From Executive Producer Emma Thompson and BAFTA-winning director Felipe Bustos Sierra comes Everybody to Kenmure Street, a multifaceted picture of one of the most memorable moments in Glasgow’s recent history.

On May 13, 2021, UK Home Office immigration enforcement launched a dawn raid in Pollokshields, one of Scotland’s most diverse neighbourhoods. Local residents rushed to the streets to stop the deportation of their neighbours. As word spread, a handful of protestors quickly grew to a crowd of hundreds, flooding Kenmure Street and completely blocking an immigration enforcement van.

The eight-hour stand-off made international headlines as the community organised itself in an extraordinary act of peaceful solidarity.

Everybody to Kenmure Street uses a combination of crowd-sourced footage from the day, archive film and dramatic re-enactments to examine the power of grassroots collective action, solidarity, and empathy in confronting state authority.
