long_description:
Dame Gillian Karawe Whitehead Hoata
Beethoven Symphony No. 9

Its audacious juxtaposition of styles, sounds and forces, including the revolutionary inclusion of a choir, marked the Ninth as a landmark work, not just for Beethoven but for music itself. Its monumental achievement and undeniable emotional power will be brought to stunning life with the help of Orpheus Choir Wellington and City Choir Dunedin.

Our essential need for community and connection is also at the heart of Dame Gillian Karawe Whitehead’s Hoata. Named for the Māori phase of the moon where the moon is barely visible, Hoata was written in 1979 during a cold northern hemisphere winter and evokes the icy blizzards and intense isolation that swirled around the composer as she wrote.

id: The Nomad 30 Year Anniversary NZ Tour-MEOW, 9 Edward St, Wellington-Event Finder
name: The Nomad 30 Year Anniversary NZ Tour
venue: MEOW, 9 Edward St, Wellington
long_description:
ReGenerate – 30 Year Anniversary NZ Tour

After three decades of making music, DJing and pushing Aotearoa’s bass culture forward, The Nomad returns to the road this October, November and early December for his national ReGenerate – 30 Year Anniversary NZ Tour.

Joined by MC Antsman and featuring immersive visuals from warpTV, the tour will bring The Nomad’s signature blend of dub, reggae, house, jungle and drum & bass to dancefloors across Aotearoa, with local support at each stop.

The tour celebrates the release of ReGenerate, a 16-track album marking 30 years of original music from one of New Zealand’s pioneering electronic artists. Beginning with Locust in 1996 and evolving into The Nomad in 1998, his journey has consistently crossed genres while remaining rooted in bass culture, experimentation and the dancefloor.

ReGenerate is more than a retrospective. It’s 30 years of sound, experience, experimentation and connection, regenerated for a new generation. Built through decades of studio production and live performance, the album reflects the sounds, people and communities that have shaped Aotearoa’s electronic music landscape.

The album will receive a deliberately limited physical release, with the complete 16-track record available on double vinyl, CD and cassette. The first pressing features just 300 copies of the double album on metallic red vinyl, making it a genuine collector’s edition. Only a selection of tracks will be released digitally, with the physical editions offering the complete album experience, from the sequencing and artwork through to the full musical journey.

Live, ReGenerate takes that history to the dancefloor. Expect heavy bass, dub, reggae, house, jungle and drum & bass, backed by MC Antsman’s energy and warpTV’s immersive visual production.

This isn’t just a DJ set. It’s 30 years of original music.

id: Mudhoney-Meow Nui, 92 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Mudhoney
venue: Meow Nui, 92 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, Wellington
long_description:
For the first time in over a decade, Mudhoney return to New Zealand for a run of intimate shows. Renowned for their ferocious live performances, the band continue to deliver the same high-voltage mix of sludgy riffs, pounding rhythms and Mark Arm's unmistakable snarl that made them one of the most influential rock bands of their era.

Formed in Seattle in 1988, Mudhoney helped define the sound that would become known as grunge, combining garage rock, punk and heavy distortion into something raw, loud and entirely their own. As one of the cornerstone acts of legendary independent label Sub Pop, the band became a crucial influence on the explosion of alternative rock that followed, with tracks like 'Touch Me I'm Sick' and 'Suck You Dry' remaining enduring underground classics.

More than 35 years on, Mudhoney remain as vital as ever, continuing to release acclaimed new music and proving night after night why they are regarded as one of the greatest live rock bands of their generation.

"When it comes to grunge, or even just Seattle, I think there was one band that made the definitive music of the time. It wasn't us or Nirvana, but Mudhoney. Nirvana delivered it to the world, but Mudhoney were the band of that time and sound." – Eddie Vedder (Pearl Jam)

A rare chance to experience genuine grunge royalty up close.

id: Old Mill Track, Aorangi Forest Park-Aorangi Forest Park, Aorangi Forest Park, Martinborough-Event Finder
name: Old Mill Track, Aorangi Forest Park
venue: Aorangi Forest Park, Aorangi Forest Park, Martinborough
long_description:
The Old Mill Track is an up and back route that runs from the Haurangi Road end to the west branch headwaters of the Tūranganui River (return).
It is approximately 4km one way (8km return), and follows a recently maintained tramping track that runs through regenerating native forest in the Aorangi Forest Park.

Transport will be provided by bus from the Martinborough town square to the Department of Conservation's Waikuku Lodge, where the walk will begin. (No access to Lodge)
Walkers will be delivered back to Martinborough town square at the end of the day.

This walk is suitable for fit trampers, with approximately 4 hours of tramping with the terrain including moderate hills to climb both up and down.

name: Midwave Breaks Album Release Tour
venue: Moon, 167 Riddiford Street, Wellington
long_description:
Midwave Breaks celebrate the release of their first full-length album, with four special shows across New Zealand.

Tauranga Alt-Rock Duo Midwave Breaks invite you to celebrate the release of their first full-length album, alongside Special Guests, with four shows across the Motu.

Since launching in 2021, Midwave Breaks have captivated fans, across airwaves and stages around New Zealand, with 8 independent radio singles hitting the NZ Top 10 Rock Airplay Charts, a nod for Best Rock Act at the 2024 Aotearoa Music Awards, and Highlight-Reel live performances in support of Incubus, Live, and Devilskin.

As a two-piece, Midwave Breaks deliver a huge sound, infectious live energy, and dynamic performance. Special guests across the tour include, The Response, The Rainfall, Courtnay and The Unholy Reverie, No Pilot, Not Exact, and Van Brookes.

Echo. Tide. Awake. is the first full-length studio album from Midwave Breaks, featuring 13 new tracks for 2026 – all written, recorded, mixed, and mastered by the band themselves, in the spare room of a farmhouse, overlooking the Bay of Plenty coastline in New Zealand. Midwave Breaks reimagine the sounds of their youth through a modern lens, epitomized by 80’s-90’s alternative rock/pop - evoking hints of Springsteen and Petty, Cornell and Vedder, and a melting pot of musical influences from past to present. Echo. Tide. Awake. explores cyclical themes of time and perspective, reframing the past to better illuminate the present.

long_description:
Authentic Indian cooking classes in Wellington with panaromic views over Wellington Harbour.

In each class, you will learn 4-5 recipes like: potato stuff roti, roasted eggplant curry, wholemeal, roti, naan; shahi paneer; dhal, samosa; palak paneer; gourmet chickpeas; vegetable korma; gulab jamun; kheer; mango lassi; masala chai, and many more...

The classes start at 6 pm or 10:30 am on weekends and weekdays with a 2-hour session followed by a dinner or lunch afterwards. There are 2 to 8 people in each class in purpose built cooking studio. Also a private cooking classes available.

The menu for the class can be:

2) Shahi Paneer (cottage cheese cubes with spices and rich tomato-cashew gravy), garlic coriander naan, cumin jeera basmati rice and sweet fragrant rice pudding with cardamom. Also I will teach how to make fresh paneer.

4) Palak paneer (creamy spinach curry with cubes of paneer), jeera rice (basmati rice with fragrant spices, panjabi chhole or spicy chickpeas curry and mango lassi. Also fresh paneer making.

5) Khadi (chickpeas fritters in yogurt and chickpeas flour soupy gravy), Aloo-Gobhi (cauliflower and potato curry),  savoury wraps with herbs and spices, fresh pickle and basmati rice.

The total cost is $130 per person, this includes ingredient cost. (As an alternative we also sell cooking class gift vouchers.The food options are unlimited and the class provides fresh and best ingredients)
Please contact for booking: indiancooking@xtra.co.nz

So just bring your taste buds! and Enjoy!!

id: "Sitting Pretty" at Ata Rangi-Ata Rangi Winery, 14 Puruatanga Rd, Martinborough-Event Finder
name: "Sitting Pretty" at Ata Rangi
venue: Ata Rangi Winery, 14 Puruatanga Rd, Martinborough
long_description:
Remember the original Toast Martinborough? Multiple vineyard visits, beautiful wines, and those long, progressive lunches that became part of the tradition? At Ata Rangi, we’re bringing a little of that magic back for one special evening.

Join us for Sitting Pretty - a sunset session celebrating Ata Rangi’s place in the old Toast Martinborough story, when our site was a stop on the festival circuit and Ruth Pretty’s much-loved food was part of the experience.

In collaboration with Rose & Smith, we’re revisiting some favourite dishes from Ruth Pretty’s menus of years gone by. Think whitebait fritters, asparagus with hollandaise, long-stemmed chocolate dipped strawberries, white crockery, linen napkins, cutlery, and the pleasure of taking your time over good food and a glass or two of Ata Rangi wine. It’s a nod to the familiar flavours and fond memories of yesteryear, and a good reason to make a few new ones.

Settle in amongst the vines, as the afternoon gives way to evening, with a relaxed yet festive atmosphere. Enjoy Ata Rangi wines, delicious food, great company and live music from Pat For President.

Whether you’re joining us to revisit a piece of the Toast Martinborough of old, or simply looking for a fun way to kick start the weekend ahead of Toast Martinborough (at The Runholder the following day), Sitting Pretty is an invitation to relax, raise a glass and celebrate where it all began.

Event details

Friday 13 November 2026
4pm–8pm
Ata Rangi, 14 Puruatanga Road, Martinborough

No tickets required, simply pay on consumption for food and beverages

id: Wellington City Chorus – Women’s Barbershop-St Andrews on the Terrace, 30 The Terrace, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Wellington City Chorus – Women’s Barbershop
venue: St Andrews on the Terrace, 30 The Terrace, Wellington
long_description:
Wellington City Chorus is a chapter of SingUnited International (formally Sweet Adelines) and was formed in 1998. This local chorus of dedicated and talented singers is a non-profit organisation dedicated to teaching, learning and singing four-part barbershop style harmony through performances and education opportunities.

Wellington City Chorus is led by co-directors David Brooks and Jo Hodgson. David is a master-director with over 30 years of experience as a singer, director, adjudicator, coach and arranger of barbershop music; Jo, a singing teacher and performer from the musical theatre and choral worlds, is a recent convert to this fun and challenging style.

As previous National champions, Wellington City Chorus has represented Aotearoa New Zealand on the international stage several times and looks forward to sharing a taste of Aotearoa in Australia next year.

We meet on Monday evenings, 7:00pm – 9:30pm at Wellington Bridge Club, 17 Tinakori Rd. We welcome women and non-binary singers who enjoy singing and are keen to learn, grow and perform in a supportive and welcoming environment.
https://www.wellingtoncitychorus.org

id: Between the Lines: Language Games with Orchestra Wellington-Ngā Pou Ruahine, Level 2, Te Matapihi, 65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Between the Lines: Language Games with Orchestra Wellington
venue: Ngā Pou Ruahine, Level 2, Te Matapihi, 65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington
long_description:
This event will take place in Ngā Pou Ruahine on Level 2 of Te Matapihi.

Between the Lines is a monthly early-evening chamber music series and book club that brings music and literature into conversation. Presented in the beautiful setting of Ngā Pou Ruahine in Te Matapihi, the series invites audiences to listen, think, and chat. No prior knowledge of music or literature is required, just a curious mind.

Taking place monthly from April to October on the final Thursday of each month, Between the Lines has been co-created by New Zealand String Quartet, Orchestra Wellington, and New Zealand School of Music. Each month these organisations will take turns presenting a talented group of musicians to perform music and host discussion on a different literary theme. From devil's bargains to language games, the obsessive tortured artist to the intimate private lives of writers and composers, this book club will delve deep into themes that span across artforms.

Each session will feature carefully selected music and a reading list highlighting the theme of the month. So, arrive solo or bring your book club to Te Matapihi for a new kind of conversation.

The theme of our October musical book club is language games.

Music to be performed: Walton – Façade

Language Games explores the joy, absurdity, and musicality of words.

In the early 20th century, artists began to break language apart and rebuild it in new ways. Meaning became fluid, rhythm took centre stage, and sound itself became a kind of play. Words were no longer just vehicles for ideas, but material to be shaped, stretched, and reimagined.

This programme draws on that spirit of experimentation. Here, language slips between sense and nonsense, clarity and confusion. Familiar patterns are disrupted, and new ones emerge. The result is something playful, unpredictable, and deeply expressive.

Music and speech meet on equal terms. Rhythm becomes meaning. Timing becomes everything. Like a poem that resists easy interpretation, the experience is not about finding a single answer, but about enjoying the movement of thought as it unfolds.

In this world, language is not fixed. It dances, it misbehaves, and it invites us to listen differently.

This event will take place in Ngā Pou Ruahine on Level 2 of Te Matapihi.
Between the Lines is a monthly early-evening chamber music series and book club that brings music and literature into conversation.
The theme of our October musical book club is language games.
Rhythm becomes meaning.
In this world, language is not fixed.

id: What is Gouache?-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
name: What is Gouache?
venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
long_description:
Come explore the versatile and expressive world of gouache in this hands-on, experimental workshop. Designed for both beginners and those looking to loosen up their painting practice, this session is an opportunity to play, experiment and discover what gouache can do.

We’ll begin with a brief introduction to the origins and history of gouache, looking at how the medium has been used across different periods and by a range of well-known artists. We’ll explore examples of gouache in practice, drawing inspiration from the distinctive ways artists have used its bold colour, opacity and versatility.

From there, we’ll get stuck into the medium through a series of playful exercises and experiments. You’ll learn the fundamentals of working with gouache — from mixing colours and exploring opacity to layering, mark-making and creating different textures — while being encouraged to develop your own approach.

Rather than focusing on creating a perfect finished painting, this workshop is about curiosity, experimentation and enjoying the process of discovering what gouache can do.

All materials included.

Thirty minute lunch break - bring a packed lunch to enjoy in our historic house or explore the local Te Aro cafes. Coffee and tea provided at lunch.

id: October Bookbinding Workshops at WCBA-Wellington Centre for Book Arts, 262 Thorndon Quay, Wellington-Event Finder
name: October Bookbinding Workshops at WCBA
venue: Wellington Centre for Book Arts, 262 Thorndon Quay, Wellington
long_description:
Saturday 24 October
Discover the Endless Possibilities of Carmencho Arregui's Crossed Structure Binding
Deceptively simple, wonderfully adaptable, and full of creative potential, the Crossed Structure Binding is a structure every bookbinder should know. Invented by Carmencho Arregui in 1992, this innovative binding transformed ideas about how books can be constructed, revealing the spine sewing and opening new pathways for both artistic and conservation work.

Working from Carmencho's diagrams and instructions, we'll explore her remarkable structure and look at examples created by binders around the world. Opening perfectly flat and capable of being adapted to soft or hard covers in materials from paper to leather, the structure offers an extraordinary range of decorative and structural possibilities. Join us to discover why this revolutionary binding continues to inspire book artists, conservators, and makers more than three decades after its invention.

Sunday 25 October
Fundamentals of Bookbinding
Start your bookbinding journey with a day dedicated to the essential skills that underpin every successful binding. You'll learn the fundamentals of cutting, folding, sewing, and gluing paper while creating a series of simple projects, including a concertina, one-sheet book, single-signature pamphlets, and, time permitting, a folded slipcase.

Along the way, you'll discover practical tips and tricks, gain hands-on experience with a range of tools, and develop a better understanding of paper and materials. The more accurately you can cut and fold, the more successful your future bindings will be. Whether you're completely new to bookbinding or looking to strengthen your core skills, this workshop provides a solid foundation for your creative journey.

Details on cost and enrolments at https://www.meetup.com/theprintingmuseum

long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Toronto International Film Festival -

James McAvoy makes his anticipated directorial debut with this wild true story of two Scottish men pretending to be Americans to achieve their dreams of hip-hop stardom.

Inspired by the real-life tale of Scottish rap duo “Silibil N’ Brains”, California Schemin’ follows lifelong friends Gavin Bain and Billy Boyd. Chasing their dream of becoming successful rappers, Gavin and Billy are faced with one problem - no one will take their aspirations seriously with their thick regional accents.

Humiliated at an audition in London, the pair return home and devise an absurd scheme: they’ll reinvent themselves as hard-partying Californian MCs, complete with elaborate backstories and convincing (enough) American accents.

Miraculously, the gambit pays off, and Sibil N’ Brains’ rise to stardom is set in motion. But as the stakes get raised, the pressure begins to fracture both their success - and their friendship.

With California Schemin’, McAvoy delivers a fast-paced, funny and poignant debut with a killer soundtrack.

long_description:
Over three sessions, create your own unique ring using the age-old lost wax technique. This is a great opportunity to spend a Friday night getting creative and making something you can wear!

In weeks one and two, you will learn how to work with jeweller’s hard wax to design and shape your own ring. Experiment with texture, form and detail to create a one-of-a-kind piece. Your finished wax ring will then be sent away for casting in the metal of your choice.

There will be a week’s break before the third session to allow time for everyone’s waxes to be cast. In the final session, you’ll learn how to trim, clean and finish your cast, transforming your wax design into an original ring ready to wear.

More advanced students can use the sessions to develop their own ring designs in a supportive class setting.

Included in the class fee are all your different types of waxes, sandpaper and courier costs.

Casting and metal costs are not included and will vary depending on the size of your ring and the metal you choose. Small castings can cost around $6.65–$12, with metal costing approximately $7–$30 depending on whether you choose red bronze, white bronze or silver.

This class is suitable for teens and children aged 12 and over. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

long_description:

This tour covers a wide range of aspects of military service of early settlers, of soldiers serving in Wellington, and of their wives and children, and the contributions those with military experience made to the development of the city, to society and to economic development.

It traverses the lower part of the cemetery, includes some of the earliest burials, and is easy walking (not suitable for those with mobility issues).

Tour duration 1.5 hours, starting and ending at the Bolton Street Cemetery Museum, lower Bolton Street.

Cost $10 per person, children under 12 free, and good dogs on leads always welcome.

id: New Zealand String Quartet presents: Legend | Wellington-Prefab Hall, 14 Jessie St, Wellington-Event Finder
name: New Zealand String Quartet presents: Legend | Wellington
venue: Prefab Hall, 14 Jessie St, Wellington
long_description:
The New Zealand String Quartet presents their 2026 Season: Storytellers.

Across a three-part Wellington series, we'll explore three distinct programmes: Origins, Transform and Legend. We’ll boldly explore more compositional voices than ever before, beginning with classical masterworks that resonate through the centuries, through to modern-day Grammy winners and the distinctive voices of Aotearoa. The three string quartets of Benjamin Britten form the heart of our 2026 Season, to mark the 50th anniversary of the composer’s death.

Storytellers showcases a rich cross-section of our society and celebrates the art of storytelling through music. Join us in 2026 as together we explore these musical stories.

PROGRAMME:
Sara Arain The Internal Eclipse
Ludwig van Beethoven String Quartet No. 11, in F minor, Op. 95 ‘Serioso’
Interval
Benjamin Britten String Quartet No. 3, in G major, Op. 94
Claire Cowan Sweet Suite: Hansel & Gretel highlights for String Quartet

The programme opens with emerging composer Sara Arain’s The Internal Eclipse, selected by the Quartet as the winning work in their competition for New Zealand School of Music – Te Kōkī students. Committed to supporting the next generation of composers, the NZSQ will perform this beautiful work - based on an ancient Persian mystical tale - across five dates on their Legend tour.   

The programme continues with Ludwig van Beethoven’s high-octane and form-breaking String Quartet No. 11, Op. 95, that continues to surprise and thrill audiences to this day.

To complete their year-long tribute to the fiftieth anniversary of Benjamin Britten’s death, the NZSQ will perform his third and final string quartet. This quietly luminous piece, based on themes from his final opera, Death in Venice, serves as a poignant musical farewell, made even more profound by the fact it was the last major work Britten ever composed.

The Quartet will bring their 2026 Season to a jubilant close with acclaimed Aotearoa composer Claire Cowan’s ‘Sweet Suite: Hansel and Gretel highlights’ - a magical reimagining of her internationally celebrated ballet score, which was the first full-length ballet composed by a New Zealand woman and enjoyed an incredible 5-week, sold-out national tour by the Royal New Zealand Ballet in 2019.

The concert programme, crafted in the NZSQ’s signature style, aims to engage audiences of all levels of familiarity with chamber music. Each piece is preceded by a friendly and informative introduction by the Quartet members, shedding light on the stories behind the music, making it an enriching experience for everyone. The NZSQ is looking forward to welcoming you all to this special evening of music and storytelling!

long_description:

The Battle of Monte Cassino was one of New Zealand’s most significant and costly campaigns of the Second World War. Military historians Chris Pugsley and Buddy Mikaere will examine the fighting, the decisions that shaped the campaign and its lasting legacy, while bringing the experience close to home through the stories of Featherston and Wairarapa servicemen who served in Italy.

id: Printing with Chine Colle-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Printing with Chine Colle
venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
long_description:
Welcome to mixed media collage the printmakers way. Chine Colle is a printing process in which a thin sheet of paper is printed on and at the same time, mounted on a sturdier sheet, creating a subtle delicate backdrop to the printed image. Expanded on, this can include contrasting papers, graphic images, select colour shapes and fabric. The mission is just to have fun creating together in the fabulous Inverlochy print studio.

In this one day workshop people will:

Practice traditional and individual chine colle techniques
Explore the use of delicate papers more responsive to ink and hand printing
Test and practice mixed media chine colle with images, papers and fabric
How effective chine colle is as a method of adding colour to prints
Making and using a damp pack
Recipes for traditional glues
Materials are supplied and feel free to bring your own special bits and bobs to include and or share.

Minimum age to attend this workshop is 16 years.

Thirty minute lunch - bring a water bottle and packed lunch to enjoy in the historic Inverlochy or explore the local cafes in Te Aro.

id: Wednesday Lost Wax Casting - 6 Weeks Course-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Wednesday Lost Wax Casting - 6 Weeks Course
venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
long_description:
A fantastic course that's full of fun and inspiration!

It starts on Wed 11 November and runs for 6 weeks till Wed 16 December, 5.30pm - 8pm.

Create interesting designs in wax, then send them off to be professionally cast in metal. Once your pieces are back, you will be taught how to cut, file and shape them into wearable pieces.

Level 1 students: Learn to work in both soft and hard jewellers' wax and send your waxes away to be cast. When they return, you will learn how to clean them up into finished jewellery and/or incorporate them into jewellery in multiple ways. We start with rings, but encourage students to think outside the box!

Level 2 students: Advance your carving skills and learn to set stones in your waxes. This can be done either by creating claws and other settings or trying the cast-in-place technique - an organic, exciting process.

Included in the class fee are all your different types of waxes, sandpaper and courier costs.

Not included are the casting and metal costs, which vary from student to student depending on what they want to make. Small castings can cost around $7 - $10, and metals are between $0.35 per gram for bronze - $4 per gram for silver. Please see details on our Regular Classes page.

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, PayPal or Afterpay on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time, please email us to arrange this ;)
